_spec.purpose: Automation-change trail. Phase 12 (AUTOMATION RETRO + UPGRADE) appends one entry per machine upgrade made after a run, both reactive fixes and frontier improvements: engine scripts, helpers, prompts, agent definitions. gmail_draft.py renders this run's entries into every dated Gmail draft so the maintainer can monitor the machine's evolution daily and pinpoint which week introduced a regression. Upgrades are committed separately (message prefix 'upgrade(<date>):') so a revert of that one commit rolls the change back cleanly.
rules: Never weaken a gate, threshold, or hard-fail rule; upgrades tighten, repair, or automate.
Every engine/script change is verified before commit (this run's slides + examples/demo-deck through render+qa, plus a defect-reconstruction test for new gates).
0-3 upgrades per run; zero is acceptable and is recorded as nothing (the email section then reads 'no changes').
Frontier improvements never displace a needed fix: the 0-3 budget fills reactive-first.

entry_schema.kind: fix (from this run's deviations) | improvement (from the frontier scan)
entry_schema.area: engine | scripts | assets | prompts | agents | knowledge
entry_schema.change: one sentence, what the machine now does differently
entry_schema.trigger: the run deviation that motivated it, or the source URL for a frontier improvement
entry_schema.verification: what was tested and the result
entry_schema.rollback: how to undo (usually: revert the named commit)

scan_log_schema.focus: which rotation area was scanned (must differ from the last 3 runs)
scan_log_schema.found: one-line summary of the most relevant findings

entries.change: New committed helper assets/js/akrelief.js: AK.reliefShade(cx, opts) turns a flat filled region into a shaded dimensional SOLID entirely in 2D ImageData, zero new deps. It builds a heightfield (noise.js fbm2/warp2 by default, or a height(u,v) callback for a dome/bevel/ridge), derives per-pixel surface normals from a 3x3 Sobel of the height, Lambert-shades against a single NW key (default) or the multidirectional oblique-weighted MDOW light set (azimuths 225/270/315/360 via {multidirectional:true}), maps a shadow->lit color ramp, and applies an optional silhouette mask (AK.reliefDome/reliefRect built in). Opt-in and unreferenced by any existing slide; text stays DOM/SVG and quantity is never encoded in the relief.

entries.change: qa.py gains glyph_ink_contamination(), a FAIL-grade detector for a label CROSSED by canvas/SVG/GL geometry, and busy_art_under_text() loses its font_px>=30 restriction so labels of ANY size are sampled. The new check samples a thin ring around every non-decorative label's glyph ink (skips 2px of anti-aliasing, out to 5px), takes the local paper value from outside that ring, and counts ring pixels closer to the GLYPH's own value than to paper. FAIL when that contaminated fraction >= 0.07 AND it spans >= 30 percent of the label's columns or rows; WARN from 0.02; data-overlap-ok demotes the FAIL to a WARN as with the DOM collision gate. It measures the DEFENSE rather than the busyness, so a knockout plate, a dark-ground scrim or a halo leaves the ring clean (a halo is the opposite value by construction) while a rule, scored outline, groove edge or GL specular running through the letterforms trips it. Documented in SKILL.md as a slide-contract rule (text over art needs a declared defense).

entries.change: TEXT UNDER AN OPAQUE PLATE is now a FAIL. render.py's in-page QA gained an occlusion probe: it collects every provably OPAQUE element box (background alpha >= 0.9 or a background image or an ; opacity >= 0.9; no blend mode; not full-bleed), intersects those boxes with each text node's LINE BOXES (ancestors and descendants skipped, so a label's own knockout plate is never its own occluder) and confirms PAINT ORDER with document.elementsFromPoint (the whole stack, topmost first, so a full-frame grain/edge overlay cannot decide the answer the way singular elementFromPoint did). A temporary '*{pointer-events:auto!important}' sheet lets the hit test see decorative layers and is removed before the screenshot. qa.py FAILs a non-decorative node when a foreign opaque plate covers >= 20x6px of a line box, WARNs at >= 12x4px, and demotes the FAIL to a WARN under data-overlap-ok.

entries.trigger: The scorer named 'dead lower zones' as the artwork-craft ceiling in SIX consecutive scored runs (entries 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18) and it was logged as a FIELD_NOTES note every time, including at the end of run 18. It was a rule in our own doctrine: 'at least one generous quiet zone per slide' had no ceiling and no address, the dossier spent it on the bottom band because that is the cheapest place, and the pixel critics grade each slide against its OWN dossier, so a slide executing a bad plan passes its acceptance checklist. entries.change: SVG LABELS ARE NOW MEASURED AGAINST THEIR OWN PLATES. render.py emits out.svg_plates: for every SVG <text> it measures containment inside the <rect> painted UNDER it (the label's knockout), reports any opaque <rect> appended AFTER it in document order (SVG has no z-index, so a plate added for the block below silently eats the line above), and asks the compositor, via document.elementsFromPoint sampled at 11 points across the label's own box, whether an opaque DOM element is painted above the whole <svg>. qa.py grades all three as FAIL, demoted to WARN under data-decorative or data-overlap-ok, with a 2px tolerance for subpixel bbox rounding on the containment case. entries.change: PLATE WIDTHS ARE NO LONGER TYPED BY HAND. New AK.svgPlate(textEl, opts) and AK.svgPlateAll(selector, opts) in assets/js/aktype.js build an SVG knockout plate FROM the label it backs: measure the laid-out text with getBBox, add padX/padY plus half of any painted stroke (getBBox excludes stroke), honour minWidth/minHeight by growing symmetrically so an anchored label stays centred, copy the label's transform so both live in one coordinate frame, and insert the rect as the text's IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING SIBLING, which is both correct SVG paint order and exactly the shape render.py's plate probe looks for. The rect carries data-plate=1 so a future gate can identify plates by declaration rather than by the last-overlapping-preceding-rect heuristic. Misuse throws a named TypeError (a page error, which render.py hard-fails) and untrimmed text console.errors (a qa.py WARN), because it measures wrong. There is deliberately NO runtime font-readiness guard: two were built and measured this run and both cried wolf on correct usage (document.fonts.status flips back to 'loading' whenever any face begins fetching, including one the label itself just triggered, warning on 3 of 4 correct calls; document.fonts.check returned false for a loaded, rendering face, warning on 4 of 4), and a guard that cannot tell correct usage from incorrect usage only teaches authors to ignore QA warnings. Awaiting document.fonts.ready stays the author's job and the svg_plates gate on the shipped pixels is what actually catches a fallback-sized plate. Documented in SKILL.md as a slide-contract rule: never type a plate width.
entries.trigger: The residual of the same deviation as the entry above (out/2026-07-29/automation_retro.md D1, D2, D3). The new gate DETECTS the defect; nothing prevented it. The authoring shape that produced it is two independently hand-typed numbers that have to agree, el('rect', {x:580, width:420}) followed by mono(594, y+32, 'ABOUT 10% OF AK PERMITS', 24), and they stop agreeing the moment anyone edits the string: revision #3 of this run's own repair CREATED a seventh instance by lengthening a legend without resizing its chip, and six render cycles went on knock-on collisions. This makes the class unreachable rather than merely detectable. Frontier corroboration from this run's typography scan: measure-then-size with an explicit padding object is settled dataviz practice (Victory backgroundPadding, the standard D3 getBBox recipe, the Vega-Lite legible-label-layout formalisation https://arxiv.org/html/2405.10953v1), and the scan corrected the primitive, since getComputedTextLength returns only the horizontal advance and ignores height and anchor while getBBox returns the laid-out box (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SVGTextContentElement) and excludes stroke (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1078743).
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION, A/B on one pair of slides. Slide A reproduces the shipped defect with three chips whose widths are hand-typed at roughly 14px per character (320, 280, 300) carrying the run's own strings at JetBrains Mono 24px / 0.10em tracking, plus a CONTROL chip hand-sized correctly at 415px: render 2/2 OK, qa.py exit 1 with 3 FAILs, 'svg label off its plate: ABOUT 10% OF AK PERMITS spills right 80px', 'ONE MARK PER PERMIT spills right 53px', 'ONE MACHINE PER 2 WKS spills right 67px', and the control silent. Confirmed by eye at full resolution: the chip's border rule runs through the 'M' of PERMITS and 'WKS' hangs off entirely, which is the shipped defect. Slide B sets the SAME strings at the SAME type spec with every plate built by AK.svgPlate and no width typed anywhere: svg_plates is EMPTY, qa fails 0, including a right-anchored label (text-anchor=end) whose plate follows the anchor and a centred label with minWidth 460 that stays centred, both confirmed by eye. REGRESSION: out/2026-07-29/slides render 9/9 OK 0 errors and qa.py WARN, 0 fails, 1 warn, per-slide identical to the shipped machine_qa.json (all nine slides load aktype.js; the addition is inert until called). examples/demo-deck renders 4/4 OK, qa 0 fails, exit 0 (it does not load aktype.js at all, so it is untouched by this change). node --check clean. No gate, threshold or hard-fail rule weakened (this adds no gate, it removes a way to fail an existing one); no new runtime dependency, vanilla offline JS, about 110 lines; no shipped slide modified. FONT-GUARD MEASUREMENT (why there is none): document.fonts.status warned on 3 of 4 correct calls and document.fonts.check on 4 of 4, so both candidate guards were removed rather than shipped as noise.

entries.change: New scripts/trend_check.py, the repeat-offender report, wired into Phase 0 step 7 and Phase 12 step 1. It reads every runs/*/score_report.json and machine_qa.json plus ledger/upgrades.json and reports three things across a window of recent runs: which rubric criterion keeps being the weakest and how many runs since an upgrade last named it, which CLASSES of hard fail have recurred, and which qa.py defect classes keep surviving into a shipped WARN. Phase 0 now plans against the standing weakness instead of discovering it at scoring. Phase 12 must now either work on the top repeat offender or state in automation_retro.md why it is deferring it again, so a deferral is visible in the dated email rather than silent. Advisory by default; --require exits 1 only on a MEASURED gap (a criterion weakest twice or more AND a countable number of runs since it was last worked on), never on a 'never worked on' row, because the last-worked column is a text match over upgrade prose and is known to under-report.
entries.trigger: Maintainer asked, after this run's retro, whether the upgrade phase was actually driven by the quality gates and repeat offenders. Measurement said no: Phase 12 closes on incidents, not patterns. Across the first 19 runs, artwork craft was the weakest criterion in 16 and was the target of exactly 2 upgrade entries, and runs 2026-07-25 and 2026-07-29 were both capped at 6.9 by the same class of defect (text against SVG or canvas geometry invisible to the DOM-only gate) four days apart, with the gate only built on the second occurrence. Nothing in the machine had ever looked across runs.
entries.verification: Run over the real 19-run corpus it independently reproduces the two findings that motivated it: artwork craft weakest 16 of 19, and 'text against geometry' flagged RECURRING across 2026-07-25 and 2026-07-29. Corpus shape drift was the hard part and is covered: 27 spellings of the top-level keys, 4 container shapes for hard_fails (list of strings, list of {rule,status} rows, the bare string 'none (all 13 rules pass)', and {'any': false, 'checked': [...]}), and glossed weakest-criterion lines. Two bugs found and fixed during testing: iterating the string form character by character invented four hard fails named n, o, n and e on 2026-07-10, and a directory of only-corrupt reports printed 'nothing to trend yet' and exited 0, which is a check that cannot see calling itself clean (now reports each unreadable file and exits 2). Determinism confirmed by byte-comparing two --json runs. Edge cases exercised: empty runs dir (exit 0), missing runs dir (exit 2), corrupt alongside good, window larger than corpus, and both --require polarities. ast.parse clean. No existing gate touched: parsers_check PASS, dossier_check PASS 9/0/0, scanner_sync exit 0, gate_status --require exit 0.

entries.area: engine (render + qa) + slide contract + dossier spec
entries.change: Slides may now declare, machine-readably on <body data-encodes='...'>, what their artwork argues without words, naming the two regions the argument lives in. render.py resolves the regions (rects or CSS selectors) and samples each with elementsFromPoint to measure how much of it is visible art rather than furniture. qa.py measures CIELAB distance and Mann-Whitney rank separability between the two populations AT 432px WIDE (the feed-scale test the doctrine already cares about) and records the numbers in machine_qa for the pixel critics and the scorer. Documented in the slide contract (SKILL.md) and as optional dossier field 11a. sRGB-to-Lab and rank AUC are written out in numpy rather than imported, so no new runtime dependency.
entries.trigger: Artwork craft has been the weakest rubric criterion in 16 of the first 19 runs. Every existing gate judges legibility; nothing judged whether the art carries the argument it claims, so a failed encoding was only ever caught by the scorer at the ship gate, too late to rebuild art. This run's own hero was the case in point: the artwork ledger called the material change at hour 7 'the thesis with zero words' and the scorer found the column read as one uniform amber extrusion.
entries.verification: SHIPPED WITHOUT A VERDICT, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS THE MAIN FINDING. Two candidate thresholds were calibrated against a real known-bad (this run's S03 steel-below-brass-above hero) and a real known-good (S07's sodium-to-slate ownership boundary, which the scorer and the flow critic both called the deck's best fusion beat). At 432px the known-bad measured dE 49.0, AUC 0.87, visible 58/83 pct; the known-good measured dE 12.2, AUC 0.77, visible 54/53 pct. Both metrics are backwards: colour separability is HIGHER on the broken encoding, and occlusion is WORSE on the working one. A threshold through those numbers passes the defect and fails the success, and a gate shipped on either would have printed 'encoding verified' over exactly the failure it was built to catch, so qa.py raises no FAIL from these numbers and the calibration table is preserved in the encoding_reads docstring. Regression: demo-deck renders 4/4 with 0 encoding rows and its pre-existing WARN/0-fails verdict unchanged, confirming the feature is genuinely opt-in; the shipped 2026-07-29 deck re-runs at WARN/0 fails unchanged; the morning's SVG-plate ground-truth slide still FAILs both its planted defects; dossier_check still PASSes 9/0/0. ast.parse clean on both engine files.
entries.rollback: Remove the out.encodings block from render.py's IN_PAGE_QA_JS and the 'encodings' key from its rec.update, delete encoding_reads plus its call site in qa.py, and drop the SKILL.md and SLIDE_DOSSIER_SPEC 11a sections. No slide currently declares data-encodes, so removal is inert.

entries.change: scripts/craft_corpus.py, the artwork-craft corpus study, plus the routing decision it forced. The script derives per-slide labels from scorer prose (with a praise veto, because the first pass read 'S6's hero RESOLVES the chronic flat-hero weakness' as a defect), computes nine objective image features over every shipped slide, and tests whether any separates the slides scorers named from the rest, with Bonferroni correction over the features tried and leave-one-deck-out stability. Because the answer was no, the wordless-claim declaration built earlier today is now routed to the reviewer who CAN judge it: dossier field 11a goes to the pixel critic, which must return encoding_reads at Phase 9, where there is still budget to rebuild art. pixel-critic.md and Phase 9 of routine_instructions updated.
entries.trigger: Maintainer asked for the corpus exercise rather than deferring it again. Artwork craft has been the weakest criterion in 16 of the first 19 runs and two prior gate attempts had failed on guessed thresholds: an absolute craft floor (2026-07-26) and colour separability on a declared encoding (2026-07-29 morning).
entries.verification: THE STUDY IS THE VERIFICATION AND ITS RESULT IS NEGATIVE, DECISIVELY. 171 slides across 19 decks, 24 labelled bad. Best feature detail_ratio at AUC 0.653 against a null standard error of 0.064, so 2.4 SE out with nine features tried; Bonferroni corrected p = 0.147; leave-one-deck-out 0.619 to 0.701, stable and stably noise; correlation with the deck's own artwork-craft score 0.15. No feature separates the groups, so an objective artwork-craft gate is NOT supportable on this corpus and none was shipped. Label derivation was audited by hand via --dump-labels and tightened after three false positives from praise sentences were found. Study output is byte-identical across runs. Regressions: parsers_check PASS, dossier_check PASS 9/0/0, gate_status --require exit 0, trend_check exit 0, all four touched Python files ast.parse clean.

entries.area: prompt + gates + scripts (the topic dedupe window)
entries.change: The topic dedupe window drops from 90 days (and the check's 120-day lookback) to 30 days, everywhere it is stated. scripts/dedupe_check.py --window now defaults to 30, prompts/routine_instructions.md states a 30-day window in the non-negotiables, the cadence note and the Phase 4 gate, config/scoring_rubric.yaml's hard fail now reads 'within 30 days', and CLAUDE.md's house rules match. A story may now be revisited after 30 days without an UPDATE reframe.
entries.trigger: MAINTAINER DIRECTIVE, given live during the 2026-07-30 run. The stated reason is that at daily cadence the topic supply is getting thin, and the maintainer's judgement is that repeating a subject after a month is acceptable. This is a LOOSENING, which Phase 12's hard rules forbid the machine from doing on its own initiative; it is logged here as human-authorized rather than machine-initiated. This run itself is evidence for the directive: the gas-curtailment story was the strongest news peg of the day and was ruled out at the gate against a 19-day-old deck, and the RTO closed-rooms story was ruled out on evidence rather than dedupe, which left the run choosing from a thinner field than the reporting supported.
entries.verification: Ran dedupe_check.py after the change; it reports 'window 30 days ending 2026-07-30' and now returns SOFT OVERLAP only where it previously returned LIKELY DUPLICATE against entries older than 30 days. Re-ran this run's own selected-candidate query and the verdict is unchanged, so the run's own editorial decision does not depend on the loosening. No other gate reads the window.

entries.area: assets (new bench) + tests (new verification) + this run's deck
entries.change: NEW assets/js/aksnow.js, the carved-snow bench. AKSNOW.surface() draws a modelled snow mass from a crest contour with (1) a ridge drawn as a LIT windward edge plus a DARK lee edge rather than a single stroke, (2) line weight that tapers along each mark and scales with depth instead of two fixed widths, (3) specular crest glints, (4) a wind-polish micro-streak population filling the space between ridges, and (5) an order-independent value ladder drawn as strips. AKSNOW.contactShadow() draws the two-part contact-plus-ambient shadow the doctrine has always specified and slides kept omitting, and it THROWS on a pure-black shadow colour. Applied to this run's deck for the drift on six slides, the S05 bench, and every pole base.
entries.trigger: The 2026-07-30 scorer's one-sentence fix, verbatim: 'Kill the repeated uniform-weight contour-line drift and build one real sastrugi surface with varying line weight, two-part contact shadows and specular crests, then apply it to S05's empty middle and S08's flat ground.' Artwork craft had been the weakest criterion in 9 of 11 runs. Four pixel critics independently described the old hatch as topographic contour lines rather than as snow.
entries.verification: tests/aksnow_verify.py renders tests/aksnow_probe.html, which draws the OLD hatch and the NEW surface over the IDENTICAL contour, palette and region, and gates four features: edge_var 3.38x (line-weight variance, the rubric's own 'uniform line weights' descriptor), orient_spread 2.27x (the old marks are all level), pair_rate 17.43x (the lit-above-dark two-edge claim, measured directly), and low_band_range, where the old hatch measures ~0 because its value ladder SATURATES at 60 percent depth and is flat for the entire bottom third, which is the 'dead lower zone' the scorer named in six consecutive runs. detail_ratio is computed and PRINTED but deliberately NOT gated, because scripts/craft_corpus.py already showed it does not separate craft (AUC 0.653, Bonferroni p 0.147) and because the old hatch wins it by drawing more level lines, which is the defect. On the real deck, lower-band tonal range improved on every measured slide (S01 +0.028, S02 +0.031, S03 +0.055, S04 +0.012, S09 +0.086). render.py 9/9 clean and qa.py 0 fails on this deck; examples/demo-deck renders 4/4 with its pre-existing warn unchanged.
entries.rollback: git revert this commit. aksnow.js is additive, so reverting only removes the bench and the probe; no existing engine path depends on it.

entries.area: gates + brand config + caption room (two rules that kept lapsing)
entries.change: caption_check.py now enforces two things that were previously prose nobody checked. (1) THE DECK SUMMARY LINE. brand.yaml has set deck_summary_line true from the start and the room stopped writing one for three consecutive runs. The linter now REQUIRES --deck-summary, verifies the declared line appears in the caption verbatim, is at least 40 characters, and is neither the hook nor the closing question. Whether the line is any good stays with the caption-critic, per the house split of geometric checks from semantic ones. (2) THE WORD 'cannot' IS BANNED in favour of "can't", house-wide, and the linter fails it. Both rules are written into brand.yaml, CAPTION_CRAFT.md, the caption-director and caption-critic agent definitions, and Phase 6 of routine_instructions.md, so the room reads them before it writes rather than being told afterwards.
entries.trigger: The deck-summary lapse was caught by the 2026-07-30 scorer, which capped Copy at 6.0 and noted it was the third consecutive run; a rule that only gets enforced by a post-hoc score deduction is not enforced. The contraction ban is a MAINTAINER DIRECTIVE given after that run ('ban the word cannot, always use can't instead, especially in the captions'). Both are TIGHTENINGS, which Phase 12 permits the machine to make on its own.
entries.verification: Ran caption_check.py against this run's shipped caption. Without --deck-summary it FAILS with an instructive message; with the declared line it PASSES at 895 chars. Reconstructed the defect both ways: a caption containing 'cannot' fails on the new VOICE rule, and a declared summary that is the closing question fails on the its-own-work rule. This run's own caption was then rewritten to carry a real deck-summary line and re-linted to PASS, and 'cannot' was removed from slide 04's body and from the first-comment block. brand.yaml still parses.
entries.rollback: git revert this commit. The gate is one flag plus one block in lint(); reverting restores the previous unenforced state.

entries.area: prompt (a queue mechanism the routine actually reads)
entries.change: NEW prompts/NEXT_RUN.md convention plus Phase 0 step 0 that reads it. A session can now queue a specific story for the NEXT run as a binding maintainer directive that overrides Phase 4 story selection. It explicitly waives NO gate: dedupe, claims, caption and scoring hard fails all still bind, and a queued story that trips the dedupe rule still has to ship as an explicit UPDATE with a material new development or not at all. The ship step archives the file into runs/<date>/next_run_brief.md so one assignment can never steer more than one run. CLAUDE.md's layout map lists it so it is discoverable.
entries.trigger: The maintainer asked, on 2026-07-30, for a specific story to be covered the following day. There was no mechanism to carry an instruction across sessions except hoping the next run's operator happened to read back through the conversation, which for an unattended daily routine means it would simply have been lost. The first queued brief is the Anthropic-employee donations story, which is also a live test of the no-waiver rule, because it duplicates No. 17 from six days earlier and has to ship as an UPDATE.
entries.verification: prompts/NEXT_RUN.md is written and Phase 0 step 0 references it by path. The brief itself states the dedupe problem, names the material new development that justifies the UPDATE, and carries the archive command. Confirmed the file is the only NEXT_RUN in the repo and that CLAUDE.md's layout section now names it. The mechanism is prose in the master prompt rather than code, which is the honest description; there is no script that can enforce 'the showrunner read the brief', and inventing one would be theatre.

entries.change: NEW committed asset assets/js/akengrave.js, a white-line intaglio engraving bench. It implements the line-engraver's four rules as code: the lay wraps the form (direction is rot90 of the height field's gradient, so the direction field IS the modelling before any value is applied), the swelled line (every stroke is a filled tapered polygon, never a stroked path), three separately controllable channels (mainline, crossline, interdot), and thickness as a per-stroke lighting decision. It also ships AKENGRAVE.reserve(), which takes MEASURED label boxes after document.fonts.ready and multiplies lay density to zero inside them with a feathered taper.
entries.trigger: Artwork craft has been the weakest scored criterion in 8 of the last 10 runs, mean 6.67, last 6.0, and it is the standing repeat offender named by scripts/trend_check.py at Phase 0. No.20's retro diagnosed why the previous fix failed, in its own words, that 'distribute the detail is a plan, not a technique, and a plan with no per-region budget gets spent on whatever is easiest to draw everywhere'. Three separately gated channels are that per-region budget expressed as a drawing system, so 'everywhere' is not an argument the function accepts. The reserve half targets the OTHER standing offender, the 'text against geometry' hard fail that hit 2026-07-25 and 2026-07-29, which qa.py structurally cannot catch because its collision walk is DOM only.
entries.verification: Rendered across all ten slides of carousel No.21 over four render passes. Final machine gate: render 10/10 OK with 0 page errors, qa.py verdict WARN with 0 fails. The engraving is visible as genuine intaglio with the lay bending around each sheet's curl and measurable stroke-width variance across every spend region, confirmed independently by five pixel critics who each transcribed and measured their assigned slides. The reserve mechanism was confirmed working by three separate critics, one of whom wrote that there is 'a clean dark bite out of the engraving exactly where each label sits, with a soft feather, and no stroke grazes a glyph anywhere on the frame'. Deck ships with ZERO knockout plates.
entries.rollback: git revert the akengrave commit. Nothing else in the engine imports it; slides opt in by including the script.

entries.change: qa.py now measures text contrast at the WORST POINT of a line rather than as a box-wide mean, so type running across a graded ground is judged by its unreadable end instead of its comfortable average.
entries.trigger: The RECURRING hard fail, text against geometry plus its contrast twin, now 3 of the last 10 runs (2026-07-25, 2026-07-29, 2026-07-31), each capping the score at 6.9. The mechanism is exact. contrast_estimate() takes one background value per node, the median of non-ink pixels across the whole bounding box, and the rubric's hard-fail rule reads 'primary text contrast below 4.5 to 1 AT WORST POINT'. The machine was measuring a mean against a rule about a minimum. On this deck, whose entire premise is a lit paper sheet under one raking key, every ground is graded by construction, and the second scorer found slide 07's ballot labels and annotations bare on the lit sheet at 3.3 to 4.4 to 1 while qa.py reported zero contrast warnings on them.
entries.verification: Defect reconstruction on the live run. Against the ten shipped renders the walk returned 5 hits and 0 fails. Three were real defects that had survived two full scoring cycles, five revision rounds, five pixel critics and two scorers, at slide 05's hero body copy (3.9 worst point against a 6.1 box mean) and slide 07's two sponsor attributions (3.7 against 4.3). Both were given a burin reserve, which the deck's own reconciliation item 5 already required, re-rendered, and the walk now returns 2 hits and 0 fails with no new plate clips or collisions on either slide. Regression on examples/demo-deck through render plus qa returned 0 worst-point hits, so flat-ground decks produce no new noise. The old contrast_estimate() is untouched and still runs; the new check can never raise a ratio the old one reported.
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-07-31) commit. contrast_worst_cell() and its five constants are self-contained and its only call site is the one block in the per-node loop, so removing them restores the previous behaviour exactly.

entries.change: render.py now scans each slide's INLINE scripts for unseeded randomness and clock reads and records them in render_report.json; qa.py FAILs Math.random / crypto.getRandomValues / crypto.randomUUID (WARNs Date.now / new Date() / performance.now), naming the file, the line number and the source line, so the determinism clause of the slide contract is enforced instead of merely stated.
entries.trigger: This run's fourth art_build defect and the only one of the five that is machine-shaped. Slide 09's 3,048-dot stipple field ran on Math.random() through five render rounds on a deck whose subject is a public RECORD, and was caught by a human running grep, not by any gate. SKILL.md has required seeded noise (AK.reseed / AK.rng, seed from the run date, 'same inputs must reproduce the same pixels') since the engine was written, and nothing enforced it. Every other check in qa.py reads ONE screenshot, so an irreproducible slide is structurally invisible to all of them: a random field is a plausible-looking field, and the defect only exists BETWEEN renders. The practical cost is that a repair round silently repaints art a pixel critic already reviewed, so the critic's note stops describing the file it was written against, and the shipped PNG cannot be rebuilt from the committed HTML.
entries.verification: Four parts, all run before commit. (1) Scanner unit cases 9 of 9: seeded AK.rng clean; bare Math.random hard; the same call inside // and /* */ comments clean; script src=... not read (so vendored d3/three/zdog never trip it); the literal string in body copy clean (DOM text is not script); type=text/template skipped; the three clock APIs soft; new Date("2026-08-01") clean; crypto.getRandomValues hard. (2) examples/demo-deck regression: render 4/4 OK and machine_qa.json BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-change baseline (0 fails, 11 warns, same messages); its flow-field and software-3D slides raise zero determinism findings, so the gate adds no noise to seeded work. (3) This run's 10 slides: render 10/10 OK, qa 0 fails and 4 warns, identical to the shipped runs/2026-08-01/machine_qa.json, zero determinism findings, and the 10 fresh PNGs are sha256-identical to all 10 shipped renders, so the deck is now provably reproducible from its committed HTML. (4) DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION: slide 09's stipple restored to the pre-fix form (AK.rng line deleted, rnd() replaced by Math.random() at both call sites); render.py printed '[determinism] slide-09.html: Math.random() line 163, Math.random() line 164' and qa.py returned verdict FAIL, exit 1, quoting both lines. Rendering that reconstructed slide TWICE produced different pixel hashes (c398e3a3d3840612 vs da7f912524b1c04e) and a drifting frame_balance number (top 87% vs 88%), which is the defect demonstrated rather than asserted. No gate, threshold or hard-fail rule was weakened: this adds one FAIL class and one WARN class and changes nothing existing. No new dependencies (stdlib re, about 90 lines).
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-08-01) commit. scan_nondeterminism() plus NONDET_HARD / NONDET_SOFT / SCRIPT_RE / _strip_js_comments are self-contained in render.py with a single call site in the render loop, and the qa.py consumer is one for-block over rec.get('nondeterminism', []) which reads an absent key as empty, so render reports written by the old renderer still parse.

entries.change: New ship gate scripts/aggregate_check.py RE-DERIVES every aggregate number a slide prints: it detects counts, durations, date spans and ratios in the rendered text, requires each one to be declared in out/<date>/aggregates.json with the claim ids it comes from, re-derives the arithmetic from claims.json, fails a count whose printed subject says STATE while a member claim is federally sourced (and vice versa), and fails a span whose endpoints are not members of the count printed in the same string; wired into gate_status.py as the 'aggregate' row and into the spec as Phase 8 step 6.
entries.trigger: This run's highest-value deviation. Slide 04 printed 'FIVE STATE POSTINGS, 22 TO 31 JUL', counting the 22 July Eielson virtual industry day (C22, eielson.af.mil) as a state posting and contradicting slide 09 of the same deck, and qa.py (PASS 0/0), copy_sync_check (PASS, 99 strings) and claims_check (PASS, 27 claims) ALL returned PASS. A pixel critic caught it by reading. The class: any on-slide string that AGGREGATES verified claims into a NEW number is itself a fresh factual assertion, and claims_check proves each claim's source while copy_sync_check proves copy.json matches the render, so nothing re-derived the arithmetic sitting on top of them. The run knew the failure mode (the fact-checker killed an 'eight days' span the same run for exactly this) and shipped one into a render anyway. The gate then found a SECOND, still-live instance in the merged deck.
files: out/2026-08-02/aggregates.json (the reference declaration set, run scratch)

(1) DETECTION on this run's real render_report.json: 18 aggregate assertions across 10 slides, with zero false positives on slide counters ('04 / 10'), on the printed scale legend ('22 PX = 1 DAY', the detector's one named exemption) or on line-break concatenations ('One state documentprints'). (2) DECLARATION set written for the shipped deck (18 entries, out/2026-08-02/aggregates.json): gate returns exactly ONE fail, and it is a LIVE ERROR nobody had flagged: "S7 'TWO DAYS EARLIER' [duration]: prints 2 days but 2026-07-30 to 2026-07-31 re-derives to 1 days" (DMV RFI published 30 Jul C11 vs transcription RFP published 31 Jul C02, both dates printed on slide 07 itself). Everything else re-derives. (3) DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION path A, the string as first rendered ('FIVE STATE POSTINGS, 22 TO 31 JUL') declared over the honest four state postings: FAILS twice, on the count (prints 5, declares 4 distinct members) and on the coupling (the span's from endpoint C22 is not one of the counted members). (4) DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION path B, the same string declared with five members including C22, which is how an incurious run would write it: FAILS on subject/source coherence, naming C22's eielson.af.mil URL against a printed subject that says STATE. Both ways of declaring the defect fail. (5) CLASS TEST, the 'eight days' span the fact-checker killed this run, reconstructed onto slide 02: FAILS, 'prints 8 days but 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-24 re-derives to 24 days'. (6) CORRECTED ARTIFACT: the same render with slide 07 reading 'ONE DAY EARLIER' and its declaration corrected returns PASS, 0 fails, 18 of 18 declared. (7) BLIND-CHECK behaviour: 18 detections with no aggregates.json FAILS rather than passing (the caption_check --ledger precedent), and a missing claims.json FAILS too. (8) ENGINE UNTOUCHED and proven: render.py on out/2026-08-02/slides 10/10 OK 0 errors 0 overflow warnings, qa.py PASS 0 fails 0 warns; render.py on examples/demo-deck 4/4 OK, qa.py WARN with 0 fails, its known baseline. No gate, threshold or hard-fail rule was weakened: this adds a gate and changes nothing existing. No new dependencies (stdlib re, json, datetime; about 480 lines with the docstring).

Two config surfaces disagreed and the gate was silent. This run's caption opens on 'Leverage' inside a verbatim quotation of the governor's own order (C13), which the scorer ruled clean on the merits, so the fix had to TIGHTEN the gate without failing a correct caption.
entries.verification: Seven cases, all before commit. (1) THIS RUN'S ACTUAL caption.txt against the captions ledger as it stood BEFORE this run's own entry: PASS, 849 chars, hook 102, with the warn "banned phrase 'leverage' appears only inside a straight-quoted verbatim passage". The correct caption still passes. (2) The same caption with quotation marks stripped: FAILS on 'leverage'. (3) The same caption with 'disrupt' inserted into ordinary prose: FAILS on 'disrupt' while still warning on the quoted 'leverage'. entries.change: NEW committed technique 92, assets/js/akhachure.js, a slope-and-aspect hachure field. One short stroke per grid cell, WIDTH from the local slope of a height field, ROTATION from the local aspect, running down the line of steepest descent, strokes longer than their cell so neighbours blend, gaussian-jittered positions, each stroke bent, and the whole field redrawn several passes at low opacity with the sun azimuth varied so shadow ACCUMULATES. Three deliberate design decisions carry the point: height() is REQUIRED and has no default, so a slide can't buy the look without the data; all randomness is normally distributed off a seeded mulberry32 rather than uniform, and there is no Math.random; and the call RETURNS ITS OWN EVIDENCE as widthRatio plus named per-region probes, so a dossier declares a number before the build and a pixel critic is asked to contradict it from the render alone.
entries.trigger: Artwork craft has been the weakest scored criterion in 8 of the last 10 runs (mean 6.25, last 6.0) with two prior upgrades aimed at it and no movement. The 2026-08-02 frontier scan named the mechanism: our detail fields are parameterised by POSITION, so a declared falloff is a gradient over an otherwise-uniform texture and no reader can see it. A hachure field is parameterised by the DATA UNDER IT, so non-uniformity is structural instead of applied. Lineage, Lehmann 1799 and https://andywoodruff.com/blog/hachures-and-sketchy-relief-maps/
entries.verification: tests/akhachure_verify.py gates four properties and PASSES: slope drives width (7.11x between a flat and a steep region against a 2.5x floor), aspect drives rotation (0.00 and 90.00 degrees on x-tilted and y-tilted fields), determinism (same seed identical, different seed differs), and height is not optional (throws without it). A RECONSTRUCTION OF THE DEFECT FAILS: a position-parameterised uniform field returns widthRatio 1.0 against the 2.5x floor. In production the slide 01 pixel critic, not told which region was which, named the heavy basin and the fine plateau correctly and called it shading rather than texture.
entries.known_limit: Width alone dies at feed scale. qa.py measured the hero's steepness encoding at AUC 0.51 and 0 percent visible at 432px. The next change is a value term so steep ground darkens as well as widens.

entries.change: Amended Phase 13 to record two things run No.25 discovered live at the delivery step. (1) THE RECIPIENT. The payload's account-relative `to` value of `me` is correct for the Gmail API but the Gmail MCP create_draft tool rejects it outright and demands a raw address, so the phase now says to pass docket@alaskaaihq.com, which is the mailbox that connector already authenticates as, and to change nothing else. It also says explicitly NOT to edit gmail_draft.py to emit the literal address, because the payload is the committed fallback artifact and `me` is right for any caller that speaks the API directly; the MCP tool is the odd one out so the workaround belongs at the call site. (2) THE PAYLOAD SIZE. The default --preview-mode grid inlines one data URI per slide and produces a ~706 KB html_body that cannot pass through a single create_draft call; the phase now directs --preview-mode remote, which yields about 17 KB and is safe because Phase 11 has already merged the raw URLs. Separately amended Phase 6 to pin three copy.json and score_report.json shapes the email reads and silently degrades without, chiefly that `aftercare` MUST be a list because gmail_draft.py renders it into <li> items and a plain string is iterated character by character.
entries.trigger: Run No.25 hit all four at the delivery step. create_draft returned 'Invalid email address' on `me`. The default payload came out at 706 KB and could not be passed. The first generated email rendered an aftercare block of about 160 one-letter bullets from a string-valued `aftercare`, printed '? / 10' because score_report.json carried the total under two alias-less keys, and printed 'None.' for the editor's note. All four were caught only by reading the generated HTML before creating the draft.
entries.verification: Amendment is prose in the master routine, so there is no code path to re-run. Verified against the artifacts of this run: the corrected copy.json aftercare list renders 5 <li> items, weighted_total 7.25 renders as '7.25 / 10 vs 8.3', editor_notes_for_email renders in full, and the remote-mode payload measured 17,282 bytes with 0 data URIs against 722,800 bytes with 10. entries.change: THE ENGINE NOW MEASURES A DECLARED CONTACT SHADOW AND FAILS AN INVISIBLE ONE. render.py gained a data-contacts probe on <body> (same rect grammar as data-encodes: a shadow region and the ground it claims to darken, [x,y,w,h] in design px, a list of rects, or a CSS selector). qa.py gained contact_reads(), which takes the median CIELAB L* of each region at 432px feed width and FAILS below 4.0 L* of separation, WARNs below 8.0, and when the ground is itself near black it names the actual fix in the failure message (light the ground first, a warm pool under the object, then cast into it). Opt-in like the encoding contract, so no existing deck's behaviour changes, but unlike encoding_reads() this one is a GATE, because the question is one-dimensional and the slide asked it itself: a FAIL is the slide contradicting its own declaration, never a taste call. Thresholds are FITTED, not guessed: the shipped defect measures dL -0.1, the mid-run repair 4.3, and slide 04's bar shadows, the ones the critics called convincing, 8.1. PHASE 7 of the routine now requires the declaration on every object that sits on something, and SKILL.md documents the contract and the silhouette corollary (a light stroke on a light object's boundary must be outside-aligned onto the dark side).
entries.trigger: The run's declared attack was the contact corollary. It was built EXACTLY as specified, #1A0F08 at alpha 0.55, and laid on a table already rendering near #0B0906, which composites to a 1.2 L* change. Four pixel critics independently returned contact_edge_reads: no, the scorer scored artwork craft 5/10 calling three of nine slides floating-adjacent, and qa.py passed the deck with 0 fails, because every gate in it judges legibility, collision, contrast or composition and none had ever asked whether a declared DEPTH CUE survived compositing. Artwork craft has now been the weakest criterion in 7 of the last 10 runs (scripts/trend_check.py --window 10).
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTED AND THE GATE FAILS IT. Built three fixture slides under out/upgrade-2026-08-05/contact-fixture/ that reproduce the run's own contact() function and palette, rendered and QA'd them. (a) known-bad, the defect as shipped: FAIL, 'shadow L* 2.6 vs ground L* 2.5, dL -0.1 at 432w -- below the 4.0 L* floor, the object floats -- the ground is already near black (L* 2.5), so there is nothing left to subtract'. NO REGRESSION ON EITHER REAL DECK: out/2026-08-05/slides re-rendered 9/9 OK and qa.py returned the identical verdict to the shipped machine_qa.json (WARN, 0 fails, 2 warns, the same two: slide 07's declared data-overlap-ok overprint and slide 09's 63 percent bottom third). examples/demo-deck re-rendered 4/4 OK and qa.py returned 11 warns and 0 fails both BEFORE the change (measured by git stash) and after. entries.change: TWO MAINTAINER WRITING RULES, both turned into gates rather than notes. (1) DATES ARE MONTH FIRST. 'August 10th', never '10 August'. The ordinal is the bare form; with a year the house writes 'August 27, 2026', which is also what the federal documents this page quotes actually print, so a quoted date and our own date look like the same language. caption_check.py fails the day-first form and a bare 'August 27' carrying neither an ordinal nor a year. (2) A COMMA BUDGET of 1.05 commas per 100 characters of caption body, hashtags excluded. The number was measured rather than guessed, from all 26 shipped captions in runs/*/caption.txt, mean 1.17 per 100 and median 1.12; the budget is ten percent under the mean, which is what was asked for. Both rules are written into config/brand.yaml (voice.do, on_slide_text_rules and linkedin_post) and knowledge/CAPTION_CRAFT.md, and both are enforced by scripts/caption_check.py, which prints the comma count, the density and how many to cut.
entries.trigger: Maintainer instruction, 2026-08-05, after reading the No.26 draft. Both rules were made mechanical because brand.yaml has a history of carrying true statements nobody enforced, most recently deck_summary_line, which lapsed for three consecutive runs while sitting in the file set to true.
entries.verification: Measured against the whole shipped corpus before writing the thresholds. Of 26 captions, 15 fail the comma budget and 11 fail the date form, so neither rule is a formality. Regex edge cases checked: 'August 27th', 'August 27, 2026' and 'August 27 2026' pass; '27 August' and a bare 'August 27' fail; 'a 27 percent cut' and 'August 2026 was quiet' do not false-positive. A compliant 618-character caption returns PASS. brand.yaml still parses.

entries.change: TWO MORE MAINTAINER VOICE RULES, gated. (1) NO FIRST PERSON IN A CAPTION, ever, outside a straight-quoted source. This needed TWO checks and that is the finding worth keeping: a pronoun grep over all 26 shipped captions returns ZERO bare hits, so by that measure the page never had a first-person problem. It had one anyway and it wore no pronoun. No.26 shipped 'No page anyone could reach shows what SEDS-AK was worth' and opened a paragraph with 'Enclosed,', which are the studio narrating its own search and its own envelope, and the first is the de-pronouned rewrite of a slide that literally says 'any page we could reach'. caption_check.py now fails the pronouns AND the named postures. Two deliberate holes so the gate does not cry wolf, 'mine' is out of the pronoun list because this page covers Graphite Creek, Red Dog and Ambler where 'the mine' is a noun, and an all-caps match longer than one character is skipped so 'the US Air Force' reads as a country. (2) NO SENTENCE OPENS WITH 'And' OR 'But'. They join clauses, so a sentence starting on one is a fragment wearing a full stop.
entries.trigger: Maintainer instruction, 2026-08-05, after reading the No.26 draft. The maintainer called it drift and was right; the run had introduced a LETTER FRAME caption whose whole posture is a sender addressing a recipient, which is first person without the pronoun.
entries.verification: Measured against the whole shipped corpus before setting anything. First person, 1 of 26 fails, and it is No.26 itself. A compliant 625-character caption returns PASS with all four of the day's new checks live. brand.yaml still parses.

entries.change: THE RUN RECORD'S GATE STATUS BLOCK IS NOW WRITTEN BY THE SCRIPT, NOT PASTED BY HAND, AND IT IS REFRESHED IN FRONT OF THE SCORER. entries.change: A DRAFTING LEADER MUST NOW SAY WHERE ITS TARGET IS, AND THE ENGINE CHECKS IT ARRIVES. A slide declares each leader, callout rule or detail-circle tail in `window.__akLeaders` as {target, at:[x,y], to:[x,y]} -- the feature's own coordinates and where the leader ends; render.py harvests the declaration into render_report.json and qa.py FAILS the slide when the two points are more than LEADER_LAND_PX (24 design px) apart, WARNs on an unusable declaration. Opt-in like the data-encodes and data-contacts contracts, so no existing deck changes behaviour, and the contract is written into SKILL.md (the slide contract read every Phase 7), DESIGN_DOCTRINE section 6.5 and the Phase 7 craft expectations.
entries.trigger: Run No.28's slide 06 shipped two drafting detail circles whose leader lines ran into empty void, past two pixel critics, a flow critic AND the first scoring cycle. The tails were authored as fixed pixel deltas from each circle's own centre (tail:[-70,-70,-150,-150]), so the target was never named in the slide, the dossier or the record and there was nothing for any reviewer or gate to check; a leader stopping in void looks exactly like a leader reaching something small.
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION: a fixture slide rebuilt from the No.28 slide 06 code (detail circle at 250,950 with tail:[-70,-70,-150,-150], target sliver at 760,470) renders and qa.py FAILS it -- "leader lands on nothing: the leader for '2024 sliver on the datum line' ends at (100,800) but that feature is declared at (760,470), 738 design px away (tolerance 24)". The repaired form of the same fixture (world-coordinate polyline terminating on the sliver) raises no leader row at all. No deck declares leaders yet, so the harvest is [] everywhere and nothing else moved. REJECTED ON THE MERITS: a pixel test of the terminus, because the leader's own landing tick puts ink where it ends, so every variant either always passes or fires on legitimate dense art.

entries.change: AN ENCODING PROBE MUST NOW SAY WHICH WAY IT READS, AND THE ENGINE CHECKS THE SLIDE AGAINST ITS OWN DECLARATION. `data-encodes` gains a required `reads` of "differ" (the two regions must be tellable apart) or "same" (an absence or sameness claim); qa.py FAILS a declaration that omits it or uses an unknown word, and FAILS a "differ" whose two regions are under ENC_DIFFER_MIN_DE (4.0 dE) apart at 432px feed width. This is NOT the quality threshold the 2026-07-29 calibration rejected and does not revisit it: the known-bad from that calibration (the steel-below-brass column, dE 49.0) still passes here, correctly, because this asks only whether the probe measured anything at all. No threshold is drawn for "same", because the corpus has no known-bad for that direction to fit one against. Opt-in preserved: a slide that declares no encoding is untouched. Contract written into SKILL.md (the slide contract read every Phase 7) and render.py's declaration comment.
entries.trigger: Run No.29's slides 05 and 06 declared the deck's central wordless claim and authored both probe rectangles from the STORYBOARD'S CAMERA ARITHMETIC instead of measuring them off a render. Re-measured off the shipped PNGs during this retro: the declared aperture rect sits at x=188 and the brightest 96x108 block actually drew at x=468 (declared-rect mean 20.4 L* against 71.8 L* on the true rect), so the probes sampled empty water about 280 design px away, reported dE 0.9 / AUC 0.58 and dE 3.5, and gate_status showed 0 FAIL rows. The deck's own build gate never gated anything; the scorer caught it at the ship gate and made it the run's one_sentence_fix. The same mechanism had already burned one probe pair earlier in the same run, reporting the DARK frame as brighter than the lit one. The light was never wrong: on the true rect the same declaration reads dE 89.9. Threshold FITTED over all 19 data-encodes lines in runs/*/machine_qa.json across 7 runs, not guessed.
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION on the real shipped slide-06 render: the declaration exactly as it shipped FAILS ('says nothing about which way it should read'); the same rects with reads:"differ" FAIL on dE 0.9 under the 4.0 floor; an unknown direction word FAILS and is named; the identical degenerate numbers declared reads:"same" return info and are correctly NOT gated. KNOWN-GOOD/KNOWN-BAD SEPARATION end to end through render.py + qa.py on a scratch copy of the deck: slide-01 (sound declaration) dE 23.7 PASS, slide-05 with the rect MEASURED off the PNG dE 89.9 PASS (was 3.5 FAIL on the predicted rect), slide-06 still on the predicted rect dE 0.9 FAIL. REGRESSION: examples/demo-deck re-rendered and re-QA'd before and after, IDENTICAL (4 slides, 0 fails, same warn set slide for slide) because it declares no encodings. This run's 9 slides re-rendered and re-QA'd: 0 fails -> 3 fails, all three on the three data-encodes slides for the declared reason, warns 16 -> 16 with no other row changed.
entries.rollback: revert the upgrade(2026-08-08) commit. Isolated to encoding_reads() plus its two constants and one branch in qa.py's main loop; the encoding contract is opt-in, so reverting restores measurement-only behaviour with no effect on any slide that declares nothing.

entries.change: THE HOUSE DATE FORM NOW SEES THE REST OF THE COPY, NOT JUST THE CAPTION. New `caption_check.py --copy out/<date>/copy.json` runs the EXISTING DATE_FORMS table over copy.json's reader-facing prose: document_title, post_copy, deck_summary_line, first_comment and every slide kicker, headline and label string. No new rule is introduced; this widens an existing gate to the surfaces CLAUDE.md always named it for. URLs are stripped before matching so no rule can fire inside a link, and every hit is reported rather than the first only. editor_notes_for_email, aftercare and caption_meta are deliberately OUT of scope with the reason written into the code: they are addressed to the maintainer in the dated draft, never to a reader, and gating a private note on public house style would train the machine to route around the gate. A --copy path that cannot be read is a FAIL, the same rule this file already applies to a missing --ledger and an unreadable brand.yaml. The failures land in caption_report.json, which gate_status.py already reads, so the completion gate picks them up with no change to gate_status.py; Phase 6 of routine_instructions.md now calls it after the style_lint pre-flight.
entries.trigger: Run No.29 shipped SEVEN bare non-ordinal dates (the incident note said six) in copy.json's first_comment, the sources block pasted under the post within 60 seconds of publishing: August 5 2026, October 16 2024, October 17 2024, June 30 2026, October 25 2025, August 8 2026, July 31 2026. The scorer caught them by eye at the ship gate. The rule was never missing: DATE_FORMS has banned the bare cardinal form since the owner set it on 2026-08-05 and CLAUDE.md names caption_check.py as the enforcement; the table simply only ever read caption.txt. Running it unchanged over the pre-repair artifact (git show 9761462:runs/2026-08-08/copy.json) catches all seven. A sweep of the whole shipped corpus finds hits in 24 of 29 runs/*/copy.json, including 16 in No.27 and 6 in No.26, both after the rule existed.
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION: the pre-repair copy.json recovered from git (9761462) FAILS with 7 DATE hits, every one in first_comment and every one correctly named with its replacement. The shipped repaired copy.json PASSES over 21 reader-facing fields. A --copy path that does not exist FAILS as a blind check rather than passing silently. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE WITHOUT THE FLAG: caption_check on this run's caption.txt with --ledger and --deck-summary and no --copy returns the identical PASS (855 chars, hook 123). FALSE-POSITIVE SWEEP: the checker was run over all 29 runs/*/copy.json and every hit inspected by hand -- all are genuine bare-cardinal or day-first dates in reader-facing prose, none is an ISO citation stamp, a URL fragment, a claim id or an editor-only field. Engine regression: render.py + qa.py re-run on examples/demo-deck (identical, 0 fails) and on this run's slides; this upgrade touches neither.
entries.rollback: revert the upgrade(2026-08-08) commit. The flag is opt-in and additive: dropping --copy from the Phase 6 call restores the previous behaviour immediately, without a code change.

The scorer wrote `threshold_used`, which was not in the alias list, so the green banner over a genuine pass read '8.02 / 10 (threshold ?)' and the maintainer's gate number was missing from the one human touchpoint.
