entries.change: AKPOST.grade now THROWS (a render hard fail) when |exposure| exceeds 0.75 stops, naming the units confusion and printing the stops value the author actually meant; akthree's AKT.setup console.errors the mirror mistake, a stops value passed to what is a MULTIPLIER on three.js toneMappingExposure.
entries.trigger: This run's deviation D1, and the same defect nine days earlier. All nine slides of No.31 authored exposure 1.02 to 1.05 meaning 'about three percent'; the library reads stops, so 2^1.03 = 2.04x shipped, a full stop over. runs/2026-08-08/slides/*.html shows all nine slides of No.30 did it too (1.0, 1.02, 1.03, 1.04, 1.05, 1.06), so eighteen consecutive slides across two runs. On No.31 it bloomed copper #B8703C until five independent critics could not separate it from gold #FFC72C at 432 px and reported it as five different faults on six slides. akpost.js documents 'stops' in its own header usage block, which is the point: a comment is not a guard, and the root cause is one word meaning two different things in two libraries the same slide loads.
entries.verification: Defect reconstruction: a slide calling AKPOST.grade(cx,{exposure:1.03,saturation:0.95,contrast:1.06}), copied from runs/2026-08-08/slide-01.html, hard-fails render.py (exit 1, page error 'exposure is in STOPS, and 1.03 stops is 2.04x the whole frame, past the 0.75-stop ceiling ... for 3 percent write 0.043'). Negative control: this run's nine slides, which use 0.03 to 0.06, all render clean and qa.py PASSes 0 fails 0 warns. Mirror check reconstructed by rendering slide-05 with AKT.setup exposure changed from 1.10 to 0.03: the console.error fires (a qa.py WARN tier) and the render still completes, which is the intended asymmetry since that direction has no shipped instance yet. examples/demo-deck declares no exposure and is unaffected.
entries.rollback: git revert 810701a. The guard is a validation branch in akpost.js and a console.error in akthree.js; reverting restores the previous silent coercion exactly.

entries.change: AK.fitText records every call's declared {min, max, maxLines} and its actual outcome on window.__akFit; render.py collects it and qa.py HARD-FAILS a block that set more lines than it declared or bottomed out at `min` without satisfying its own constraint.
entries.trigger: This run's deviation D2. Slides 02, 03, 05, 06 and 08 all ran past their declared line counts because `min` was authored higher than the box width could ever hold, two numbers chosen independently that have to agree. On slide 08 the three-line clamp swallowed 'It is for the grid.', the sentence carrying the deck's whole thesis, and the slide shipped arguing only the negative half of its own argument through machine QA, two pixel-critic rounds and a flow critic. aktype.js has set data-fit-overflow='1' on the element since the helper was written and `grep -rn fit-overflow --include=*.py --include=*.js .` returns three hits, all three inside aktype.js: nothing has ever read it, so an explicitly declared constraint has been failing in silence for the life of the engine.
entries.verification: Defect reconstruction: an h1 in a 420px box with {min:52, max:84, maxLines:3}, the shape of slide 08's failure, FAILS with 'AK.fitText bottomed out on hl: it set 4 lines against maxLines 3, at 52px (min 52, max 84)'. Negative control: this run's final nine slides produce 8 fit records, every one fit:true with lines equal to its declared maxLines, and slide 08's record now carries all three sentences including 'It is for the grid.'; qa.py PASS 0 fails 0 warns. examples/demo-deck calls fitText nowhere, reports zero fit records and is unchanged at 0 fails and 11 warns. Not opt-in, and a false positive is structurally impossible: fit:false means the binary search bottomed out and `min` itself did not satisfy the author's own constraint. overflow_y is recorded but deliberately not narrated in the failure message, because fitText only enforces height on a box the author capped and every normal auto-height block reports it true.
entries.rollback: git revert 810701a. The register is additive (window.__akFit), render.py reads it defensively and qa.py uses rec.get('fits', []), so an older render_report.json is still gradeable after either direction.

entries.change: New opt-in slide contract window.__akAssert = [{what, expect, actual, tol, unit}]: the slide states what its type claims and what its geometry computed, and qa.py FAILS when the two are further apart than the declared tolerance.
entries.trigger: This run's deviations D3 and D4. Slide 05 printed an 840 px dimension rule that was exact to the pixel over a scene whose two masses were 266 px apart, so the deck's one load-bearing measurement, twenty feet, was drawn as about six, and every gate passed it; it took a forensic human read to catch. The same run printed two map frame widths as typed constants that were wrong by 7 and 25 percent against the projections that actually drew the maps. One defect in two costumes: a number in type and the geometry it names, computed independently. The run also found the answer by accident, in slide 07's window.__akMarkCount, which caught 189 and then 196 before landing on an exact 200 but only console.error'd, so it worked because a human was watching. This promotes that pattern to a FAIL and generalises it.
entries.verification: Defect reconstruction: a slide drawing its two masses at x=300 and x=566, printing 'TWENTY FEET, 840 PX' and declaring {expect:840, actual:266, tol:4}, FAILS with 'the slide claims 840 px and the drawing produced 266 px, 574 px apart against a declared tolerance of 4 px' -- run No.31's actual numbers. Negative controls: this run's nine slides declare no assertions, report an empty list and are not judged (qa.py PASS 0/0); examples/demo-deck likewise. Unusable declarations (no `what`, non-numeric expect/actual, missing `tol`) WARN rather than FAIL, so a malformed declaration can never be read as a silent pass. Pure arithmetic on two numbers the slide supplied, so it cannot speak about art it does not understand. SKILL.md states the better answer first: derive the type FROM the geometry (slide 05's rig is now solved from the lock, one world unit is one foot at 42 px) and declare the assertion to prove the derivation survives the next edit.
entries.rollback: git revert 810701a. Opt-in and additive; no slide in the corpus declares __akAssert, so reverting changes no existing verdict.

entries.change: Canvas text is now measured where it lands, and qa.py FAILS a string that runs off the frame. render.py's init-script hook already recorded every fillText/strokeText string; it now also records the draw coordinates, the measured advance, textAlign, the active transform and the canvas size, and computes the string's device-space left and right edges. qa.py adds a canvas-bounds check that fails when a meaningful string (4 or more alphabetic characters) ends past the right edge or starts left of the frame.
entries.trigger: Run No.32 slide 08 shipped the label 'MORE THAN 20. TWO READS DISAGREED. C28' starting at x 830 with 38 characters to draw in 250px. The render printed 'MORE THAN 20. TWO READS DISA'. The severed string was the deck's uncertainty disclosure, the sentence explaining why the slide says 'more than 20' instead of a count, so its loss made the deck look like it was asserting a number it had deliberately refused to assert. Canvas has no layout engine, so nothing overflowed and nothing errored. render.py reported 0 page errors, qa.py reported 0 fails, copy_sync_check passed because it only inspects DOM, and aggregate_check passed because the authored string was correct. The scorer caught it by eye and named the gate as the fix.
entries.verification: Reconstruction of the defect FAILS as designed: a fixture reproducing slide 08's original label position reports 'canvas text runs off the frame ... ends 147px past the right edge and is CLIPPED', verdict FAIL. The repaired run No.32 deck renders 9/9 with 0 fails under the new gate. examples/demo-deck renders 4/4 and stays at WARN with no bounds fails, so no false positive on the bespoke reference. Skewed, rotated and mirrored transforms are skipped by construction, which is why slide 01's mirrored relief type and slides 06/07/09's rotated proof sheets do not trip it.
entries.rollback: git revert the upgrade(2026-08-13) commit. The hook fields are additive and default to absent, so an older render_report still parses and the check simply skips entries without dev_right.
entries.limits: It sees the FRAME boundary only. Text intentionally cropped by a clip() region is invisible to it, and so is text that collides with another object without leaving the canvas. It judges only axis-aligned positively-scaled text, where the device-space span is exact.

entries.change: A LEADER NOW HAS TO ARRIVE AT WORDS, NOT JUST AT ITS TARGET. The window.__akLeaders contract gains two required fields, `from` (the point where the line meets its label) and `label` (that annotation text verbatim), and qa.py FAILS a leader that declares neither, that names a label no rendered text on the slide reads, or whose label is drawn more than LEADER_LABEL_PX (32 design px) from where the line arrives.
entries.trigger: This run's deviation 7, found by the scorer and by nothing else. Three annotation elements shipped with no terminal value at all: S01's leader ran off the Rhode Island ring into bare sheet, S07's dimension call printed none of the values its own dossier type spec declared, and S08's correction-stamp leader descended into empty paper. The pixel round claimed to fix leaders on 01, 06 and 08 and only 06's was really fixed. machine_qa returned PASS at 0 fails and 0 warns, and the 2026-08-07 leader gate returned ok on all three, because the contract named the FEATURE end only and all three landed on their features perfectly. Every one of this run's five leaders was authored with `to` identical or near identical to `at`, which is the tell: the gate was checking the end nobody gets wrong. A leader is a sentence with two ends and half of it had never been anybody's job.
entries.verification: Three fixtures built from this run's own shipped geometry, rendered and graded through the real pipeline. (1) DEFECT AS SHIPPED: slide 01's leader, declared honestly with from:[520,1006] and label 'RHODE ISLAND AT TRUE RELATIVE SCALE', FAILS with 'no text on the slide reads that, so the line ends in bare sheet'. (2) LABEL REAL BUT ELSEWHERE: the same leader declaring the slide's real footer string FAILS with 'arrives at (520,1006) but its label is drawn 150 design px away (tolerance 32)'. (3) NEGATIVE CONTROL, the one leader this run built correctly: slide 06's, declared from:[560,624] label 'RINGS OVERLAP FROM HERE', passes at 0 fails and records 'meets its label 5.0px away'. The 5 px true gap against the 150 px true miss is where 32 comes from. Regression: examples/demo-deck renders 4/4 and stays at 0 fails, 11 warns, exit 0, its documented baseline, since it declares no leaders. Re-rendering this run's nine shipped slides now reports 5 fails on the 4 leader slides, which is the gate reproducing the scorer's finding on the real deck plus the two undeclared leaders on 06 and 07; the shipped artifacts were not modified. render.py's in-page JS is node --check clean and both scripts ast.parse clean.
entries.rollback: git revert the upgrade(2026-08-14) commit. The two fields are additive on the render side and a report written before them carries no `from` or `label`, so an older render_report still parses; reverting returns the leader verdict to the target end only.
entries.limits: Position is verified against DOM and SVG text boxes. A label found only among the canvas fillText strings has its existence confirmed and its position WARNed as unverifiable, because the canvas-text hook records a horizontal span and no line box. Retiring that limit is parked with its arithmetic and its in-container probe in knowledge/FIELD_NOTES.md, 2026-08-14. A slide that declares no leaders at all is still judged on nothing, which is the standing property of every opt-in contract here.

entries.change: THE PNG A GATE GRADES IS NOW PROVEN TO BE THE PNG THAT SOURCE MAKES. render.py records the SHA1 of each slide's source file next to the record it wrote, prints STALE for any slide whose file has moved on since, and qa.py HARD-FAILS that slide.
entries.trigger: This run's deviation 6. Two projection-note repairs were applied to source and then not re-rendered, because the render call that followed named a different `--only` subset. Both were silent no-ops, the flow critic read the pre-repair contact sheet and reported both repairs as still broken, and a whole critic round was spent on a picture that no longer existed. `--only` is a sharp tool and nothing anywhere in the pipeline could tell a PNG that matched its source from one that did not, so the only available check was somebody remembering which numbers they had typed.
entries.verification: Defect reconstruction in the run's own shape: render two slides clean (qa PASS 0/0), edit slide 02's source, then re-render `--only 1`. render.py prints 'STALE: slide-02.html changed since its PNG was made' and qa.py FAILS slide 02 with 'stale render, slide-02.html has been edited since this PNG was made, so every judgement on this slide is about a picture that no longer exists', verdict FAIL. Re-rendering `--only 2` returns both slides to PASS, so the gate clears the moment the operator does the thing it asked for. Regression: this run's nine shipped slides re-render and carry matching hashes (no stale fail anywhere), examples/demo-deck renders 4/4 at 0 fails 11 warns exit 0, unchanged. scripts/copy_sync_check.py reads the new report shape and still returns PASS on 86 authored strings. Two hashes compared, so a false positive is structurally impossible.
entries.rollback: git revert the upgrade(2026-08-14) commit. The `source` block is additive and qa.py skips any record that has none, so a report written before this exists is still gradeable in either direction.
entries.limits: It sees the slide HTML only. An edit to a shared asset under assets/js, to a font, or to a data file the slide reads leaves the slide's own hash unchanged and is invisible here. A missing or unreadable source WARNs rather than FAILs, because a moved render directory is not a stale render.

entries.change: THE CAPTION LEDGER'S BURN LIST NOW ARRIVES BEFORE THE ASSIGNMENT, AND A NEW: CLOSE HAS TO BE NEW. New `caption_check.py --burns ledger/captions.json` prints what the divergence windows forbid today, every closing move ever shipped with its use count and dates, and the ledger's own notes that say a move is burned; Phase 6 step 1 now runs it and pastes it into both director assignments. Separately, when `--copy` and `--ledger` are both given, the room's declared caption_meta is graded against the ledger's own windows, and a closing move labelled NEW: that repeats a move already shipped is a FAIL.
entries.trigger: This run's deviation 2, the fifth occurrence of one failure. The caption-critic killed candidate A because its price close was burned on 2026-07-30, restated on 2026-08-06, and phrased as the 2026-07-24 close with the nouns swapped. The showrunner's brief barred only the previous run's close. The information was never missing, it lives in these entries and in their free-text notes, and the brief was written without reading it. The ledger's `_spec` has carried the divergence windows for 33 runs with nothing mechanical reading them. And the run then shipped NEW:SUFFICIENCY TEST nine days after No.26 shipped NEW:SUFFICIENCY TEST, so a claim of novelty was the one declaration in this machine with nothing behind it.
entries.verification: Defect reconstruction on the real artifacts. Against the ledger as it stood at Phase 6 time (this run's entry removed), `caption_check.py out/2026-08-14/caption.txt --ledger <pre-ship ledger> --copy out/2026-08-14/copy.json --deck-summary ...` FAILS with exactly one fail, 'the closing move is declared NEW (NEW:SUFFICIENCY TEST) and the same move already shipped on 2026-08-05, so the claim is false'. Negative controls: runs 2026-08-13, 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-09, each graded against the ledger truncated to before its own date, all three PASS, so the window checks fire on the defect and not on legitimate divergence. `--burns` prints the table deterministically and its NOTES THAT SAY BURNED section surfaces the 2026-07-30 PRICE burn verbatim, which is the sentence the brief needed. No existing gate, threshold or window was changed: the windows enforced are the ones ledger/captions.json has always written down, and the NEW: check enforces what the NEW: label already claims.
entries.rollback: git revert the upgrade(2026-08-14) commit. `--burns` is a new subcommand and the caption_meta grading only runs when --copy and --ledger are both passed, so every existing invocation behaves exactly as before.
entries.limits: It grades the DECLARED move labels, not the prose. Run No.33's candidate A was also the 2026-07-24 close with the nouns swapped, and no mechanical check here sees that; the caption-critic remains the only reader of phrasing. The burn table is a briefing, and reading it stays a human step.

entries.change: BESPOKE_CHECK CAN SEE MODULE SCRIPTS. Both of the two places bespoke_check.py extracted a slide's art code matched the literal pattern `<script>` with no attributes, so every slide that loads akthree, and therefore every deck that climbs to rung 1 of the rendered ladder, was measured on its <div> list alone with ZERO inline script read. Both regexes are now attribute-tolerant, `<script(?:\s[^>]*)?>`; src-only tags are still stripped by HARNESS above, so a vendored library is never counted as the deck's own drawing.
entries.trigger: This deck reported FAIL at 0.810 median pairwise similarity with a drawn share of 0 percent, 0 drawn marks against 0 blocky ones. Zero against zero is not a measurement of anything, which is the signature of a checker that cannot see rather than of a deck that is templated. The engine's own SKILL.md REQUIRES `<script type="module">` for akthree, so the gate was blind to exactly the decks it most needed to read.
entries.verification: The reference deck examples/demo-deck is unchanged by the repair: PASS, 0.071 median, max pair 0.099, drawn share 82 percent (9 drawn vs 2 blocky). This deck moved from a false FAIL at 0.810 median / 0 percent drawn to an honest WARN at 0.368 median, max pair 0.696, drawn share 72 percent (158 drawn vs 62 blocky).
entries.rollback: Revert the single upgrade(2026-08-15) commit. The two regexes return to the literal `<script>` form and every akthree deck is again measured on its <div> list alone.
entries.limits: It fixes what the checker READS, not how it scores. The similarity thresholds (FAIL_MEDIAN 0.60, FAIL_PAIR 0.95, FAIL_DRAWN_SHARE 0.45) are untouched, and they were calibrated against decks whose art code the checker could actually see, so they have never been exercised against a module-script deck's true numbers. Watch whether 0.60 is still the right median for GPU decks over the next few runs before trusting a near-threshold pass.

entries.change: A CAPTION NO LONGER COLLIDES WITH ITSELF. caption_check.py's variety engine now drops ledger rows whose run_date equals the run directory being checked, before comparing opening words and moves.
entries.trigger: The documented ship order appends this run's row to ledger/captions.json and only THEN runs the completion gate, so from that moment caption_check compared the caption against its own row and hard-failed with 'first words repeat the 2026-08-15 caption'. It fired on the one gate the ship cannot proceed past, and it would have fired on every future run in exactly the same place.
entries.verification: Loosens nothing: one run writes one caption, so no honest repeat can carry today's date. Verified both directions. This run's caption goes FAIL -> PASS with the ledger row present, and a regression copy of the same caption placed under a 2026-09-01 run directory still hard-fails with 'first words repeat the 2026-08-15 caption', proving a genuine cross-date repeat is still caught.
entries.rollback: Revert the single upgrade(2026-08-15) commit. caption_check compares against every ledger row again, including the run's own.
entries.limits: The exclusion is keyed off the run DIRECTORY name matching YYYY-MM-DD, which is how every run directory in this repo is named. A caption checked from stdin, or from a directory not named for its date, is compared against the full ledger exactly as before, so the guard fails safe rather than silently widening.

entries.change: THE PHRASE GATE NOW READS THE SLIDES. New caption_check.check_copy_phrases() runs brand.yaml's banned_phrases over every reader-facing string in copy.json, the same fields check_copy_dates already walks, with the same straight-quoted-verbatim exemption. And gate_status's caption row now HARD FAILS on a caption_report.json written without --copy, detected by the absence of copy_fields_checked, which is written only on that path.
entries.trigger: The phrase gate had only ever read the CAPTION. Slide 02 printed 'a coordinated, actionable plan' in the deck's own unquoted voice and 'actionable' is item 46 of the list, so a hard fail travelled through every gate in the run and was caught by the scorer, one phase from the email. The second half matters as much as the first: gate_status only READS caption_report.json, so a run that invoked caption_check without --copy got a green caption row while the slide bodies had never been scanned at all. A gate nobody is required to point at the evidence is not a gate.
entries.verification: Verified both directions on this run's own copy.json. The repaired wording passes; restoring the original unquoted 'a coordinated, actionable plan' produces FAIL: PHRASE: banned phrase 'actionable' in copy.json slides[1].body. Running it for the first time on this run also caught three bare 'August 5/10/15, 2026' dates in first_comment that the house ordinal rule forbids and that nothing had ever checked, all three now fixed.
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-08-15) phrase-gate commit. copy.json's slide bodies go unscanned for banned phrases again and gate_status accepts a caption report written without --copy.
entries.limits: It scans copy.json, not the rendered pixels, so a string that reaches a slide without passing through copy.json is still unscanned. copy_sync_check is what ties the two together, and it is a separate gate; if that one is ever weakened, this one narrows with it.

entries.change: A RUN CANNOT STOP ON A LOW SCORE ANY MORE. New scripts/ship_gate.py exits non-zero when a run reaches the ship step with score.ship false, prints the scorer weakest criterion and one_sentence_fix as the work order for the next round, and is wired in as a gate_status row. gate_status score row changed from WARN to FAIL for the same reason. Degradation ladder step (d) now requires out/<date>/NO_DECK.md whose first line begins BLOCKER:, and the gate REFUSES that file when six or more slides rendered, because a deck that rendered is a deck. The rule is written into CLAUDE.md and prompts/routine_instructions.md beside the 2026-08-08 incident.
entries.trigger: This run scored 7.51 against 8.3 and the showrunner wrote an honest post-mortem, mailed a DO NOT POST draft, left the PR unmerged and stopped, with nine finished slides on disk, every machine gate green and the scorer own finite list of defects unfixed. Every artifact was truthful, which is what made it dangerous: the 2026-08-08 failure announced itself with an essay about integrity, and this one announced itself with an immaculate failure report. Nothing in the machine objected, because nothing had ever been asked to.
entries.verification: Four cases, all checked. A run at 7.51 vs 8.3 exits 1 and prints the four lowest criteria by weight. A run at 8.55 exits 0. A NO_DECK.md written over a nine-slide rendered deck is REFUSED with exit 1 and told to delete it and iterate. A NO_DECK.md with a real blocker and no renders exits 2 and is allowed. gate_status now shows both score and ship_gate as FAIL rows on this run, which is the correct reading of it.
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-08-15) ship-gate commit and delete scripts/ship_gate.py. A run may then stop below threshold again with nothing objecting.
entries.limits: It gates STOPPING, not quality. It cannot tell a run that iterated well from one that iterated badly, and a run determined to end can still write a false BLOCKER line, though it can no longer do so with a rendered deck on disk. It also cannot fire if the scorer is never run at all; that case is caught by the existing missing-score_report row.

entries.change: THE ON-SLIDE TEXT RULES NOW RUN ON ON-SLIDE TEXT. Two changes to caption_check.py, one shape and one rule. (1) copy_prose() walked a slide only when its value was a DICT, so a copy.json whose slides are LISTS OF STRINGS -- the shape the copy room actually writes -- contributed nothing at all, and this run reported copy_fields_checked 4, the caption-side prose fields only. It now recurses through dicts, lists and nested lists, so the date table and the banned-phrase pass finally reach the strings set in type on the artwork: 4 fields checked became 47 on this run's own copy.json. (2) New check_slide_openers() enforces brand.yaml's 'No slide string opens with And or But' (maintainer, 2026-08-05), which was written twice in config/brand.yaml and had no code anywhere. Editor-only fields (editor_notes_for_email, aftercare, caption_meta) stay out of scope exactly as before, and only the HEAD of a slide string is tested, because the rule is about opening.
entries.trigger: The scorer caught slide 06 shipping the kicker 'AND FOURTEEN MORE' by reading the pixels, and capped a raw 8.52 at 6.90. An explicit maintainer rule about ON-SLIDE text was enforced on everything except on-slide text, and the two gates that were supposed to cover the slides (the 2026-08-08 date widening and the 2026-08-15 phrase widening) had been silently walking past every slide in the file for a shape reason nobody had noticed. This is the most expensive machine gap in the run.
entries.verification: (1) RECONSTRUCTION of the shipped defect: this run's real copy.json with S6[0] restored to 'AND FOURTEEN MORE' PASSES on HEAD (exit 0) and FAILS now (exit 1), naming the field, the rule and both brand.yaml locations. (2) THE WIDENING PROVED, not assumed: a banned phrase ('game-changer') and a day-first date ('7 August, 2026') injected into two slide strings are INVISIBLE to HEAD (exit 0, zero fails) and are both caught now. (3) FALSE-POSITIVE CONTROL: a slide string reading 'Nineteen projects, and fourteen more' is not flagged, because only the opening of a string is tested. (4) This run's actual shipped copy.json, which the showrunner has already repaired, PASSES the new gate at 47 fields checked with zero new fails, so the widening does not light up correct copy. (5) caption_check on this run's caption.txt is unchanged: PASS, 863 chars, hook 102.
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-08-16) commit. copy_prose stops recursing (slides go unread again for list-shaped copy.json) and the opener rule loses its only implementation.
entries.limits: It reads copy.json, not the rendered slide, so a string hand-edited into the HTML during pixel review and never synced back is still only caught by copy_sync_check's own comparison. The opener rule tests the head of a string, so a two-sentence slide body whose SECOND sentence opens on a conjunction is not flagged; that is the rule as written. The other on_slide_text_rules (colons, first person) remain unenforced and are the obvious next widening.

entries.change: THE RENDER REPORT NOW RECORDS EVERY TEXT NODE, NOT THE FIRST 80 CHARACTERS OF THEIR JOIN. Each DOM element's direct text nodes are recorded separately as `texts` (200 chars each, 12 max) beside the existing joined-and-truncated `text`, and copy_sync_check builds its blob from both. Nothing that reads `text` changes.
entries.trigger:
Slide 09 set three fact lines in one div with
s. render.py recorded the element as one joined string cut at 80 characters, so the third line was invisible to copy_sync_check, which reported a FALSE FAIL on copy that was on the page. The run worked around it by splitting the div into three elements; the reporting hole stayed open.
entries.verification:
RECONSTRUCTION of the exact defect: a slide with three fact lines in one
-separated div, and a copy.json listing all three. HEAD render.py + HEAD copy_sync_check: FAIL, 2 of 3 lines 'not found in the render', exit 1. New render.py + new copy_sync_check: PASS, 4 of 4 strings present, exit 0. NEGATIVE CONTROL: with one label altered to a date the page does not carry, the new check still FAILS and names it, so nothing about matching was relaxed. Both decks re-rendered with the new report shape and re-gated: run35 PASS 0/0 and demo WARN 0 fails / 5 warns, both identical to baseline.
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-08-16) commit. The report loses `texts` and copy_sync_check falls back to `text` alone (its blob builder tolerates the field being absent, so an old report still checks).
entries.limits: A single text node longer than 200 characters is still truncated; copy_sync_check's existing 40-character leading-window rule covers that case, as it always did.

entries.change: THE AXIS CENSUS: A MARK ON A MEASURED AXIS IS A QUANTITY, WHATEVER IT WAS DRAWN FOR. A slide whose artwork carries a number in a POSITION declares <body data-scale> with from/to as [design px, value], the band the scale owns, and every mark in that band with what it means. qa.py FAILs a mark that declares no meaning, a mark outside its own span, and any run of ink in the band, at least as strong as the weakest mark the slide itself declared, that the slide does not declare, printing the VALUE that position reads as. Opt-in like the encoding and contact contracts; a slide that declares no scale is not judged.
entries.trigger: This deck shipped the defect twice through every green gate. Slide 07 hung three gold place ticks under a rail whose x means DOLLARS, so three REGIONS were printed at three dollar amounts. Slide 02 set thirteen division ticks on a money rail, implying twelve equal months across a budget period that runs ten. Both were caught by a pixel critic reading the picture, and nothing mechanical could have caught either, because nothing in the run ever wrote down that the axis was quantitative or what was sitting on it.
entries.verification: (1) RECONSTRUCTION of the run No.35 defect: a dollar rail declaring two marks with three undeclared place ticks drawn on it FAILS, naming 430 (reads as 97,703,794 dollars), 520 (129,108,586) and 610 (160,513,377). (2) POSITIVE CONTROL: the same slide with all five marks declared PASSES, census 'finds no others'. (3) The three extras declared with an empty `means` FAIL on the no-meaning rule, with their dollar values printed. (4) REAL ARTWORK, the strongest test: this run's own slide 04 (a rail with five $50M ticks hanging into a stippled plain) was given a hand-written declaration of its five ticks. The census found exactly ONE undeclared mark, the lit notch at the rail's left end, which is a real mark on that axis and the slide's central quantity. Declaring the notch too: PASS, 0 fails 0 warns, 6 declared marks and no others found. (5) Both decks re-rendered and re-gated with the change in: run35 PASS 0/0, demo WARN 0 fails / 5 warns, both byte-identical to baseline (neither declares a scale, so the census is silent).
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-08-16) commit. data-scale becomes an ignored attribute and the census disappears; no slide depends on it.
entries.limits: It is CALIBRATED ON THE SLIDE'S OWN INK and built to under-report: the detection threshold is the weakest DECLARED mark's own ink, measured as the median down the band so a mark that crosses the band scores and a texture field does not. A mark fainter than your weakest declared mark is not found, and a scale that declares NO marks gets an info line and no census, because there is nothing to calibrate against. It assumes the axis is linear between `from` and `to`; a log axis must not declare one. It cannot see a mark drawn outside the declared band, which is the intended escape hatch for ornament.

entries.change: aggregate_check.py NOW REGISTERS EACH CLAIM UNDER BOTH ITS "id" AND ITS "claim_id", so an aggregate's member/from_claim reference resolves whichever field name the fact-checker wrote. The claims lookup table is built with claims.setdefault(str(key), c) over both non-None keys instead of str(c.get("id")) alone. Matching, verification and cross-check logic are untouched.
entries.trigger: Run No.36 deviation: this run's claims.json emitted only "claim_id" (no "id"), so aggregate_check keyed every claim under the string "None" and EVERY aggregate member/from_claim lookup failed with 'member not in claims.json', while claims_check (which reads claim_id) stayed green. The showrunner worked around it in-run by mirroring claim_id into id in claims.json; the gate's blind spot to the field name stayed open.
entries.verification: (1) RECONSTRUCTION of the exact defect: this run's real aggregates.json + render_report.json with a claims.json stripped to claim_id only (the pre-workaround state). HEAD aggregate_check FAILS -- S3 member 'c7' not in claims.json, S6 member c13 not in claims.json, plus three cascading 'item not in the text of the declared claim(s)' fails. Fixed aggregate_check on identical inputs PASSES, 3 detected / 3 declared. (2) BACKWARD COMPAT: same run with claim_id stripped (id only) PASSES. (3) REAL SHIPPED RUN out/2026-08-18 (both fields present) PASSES 3/3, unchanged from ship. (4) NEGATIVE CONTROL (gate not weakened): a real member id renamed to a bogus 'cZZ' still FAILS and names 'member c7 is not in claims.json', so a genuinely missing member is still caught. (5) py_compile clean.
entries.rollback: Revert the upgrade(2026-08-18) commit. The lookup falls back to keying by id alone; a claims.json that carries id (the current fact-checker output does, after this run's workaround) is unaffected.
entries.limits: Populates the lookup more completely only; it does not reconcile a claim that carries id and claim_id with DIFFERENT values (setdefault keeps the first registered under each distinct key, so both names point at their own claim object -- the intended behavior). It does not change what the fact-checker emits; a separate normalization at claims-emit time remains a cleaner long-term shape and is out of this phase's scope.

entries.change: THE EMPHASIS MAY OPEN BEFORE THE NUMBER. dossier_check.py's field-4a pattern now consumes an optional leading ** or __ before the field number, so `**4a. Lower-third treatment.**` is found as well as `4a. **Lower-third treatment.**`. Nothing else about the field changes: the 200-character thinness floor, the modeled-tone test and the breather hatch all run exactly as before, on a field the gate can now see.
entries.trigger: Run No.37 deviation: all nine dossiers were authored `**4a. Lower-third treatment.**`, which is what SLIDE_DOSSIER_SPEC's own line 34 looks like when an author bolds the whole label, and dossier_check FAILED 9 of 9 with 'no field 4a', the least informative failure this gate can produce. It cost a full authoring pass to re-format nine paragraphs that were already correct. This is a repair and not a loosening: a field the gate can't FIND is a blanket fail with no information in it, and finding it is what subjects it to the tests that are the actual gate.
entries.verification: RECONSTRUCTION of the exact defect, this run's storyboard rewritten to the form the run actually authored: HEAD dossier_check FAILS 9 of 9 'no field 4a', exit 1; new dossier_check PASSES 9 of 9, exit 0. NEGATIVE CONTROLS in the new form: a 28-character field 4a still FAILS on the 200-character floor, and a 200-plus-character field naming only plate, hairline, rule, caption, footer, fixture, label, counter and chip still FAILS on modeled tone with the flat furniture named. BACK CATALOGUE: runs/2026-08-13, -14, -15, -16 and -18 all still PASS 9 of 9, unchanged. Engine untouched; render.py + qa.py re-run anyway on this run's nine slides (9/9 OK, qa PASS 0 fails 0 warns) and on examples/demo-deck (4/4 OK, qa WARN with its usual busy-art and touching-glyph warns).

entries.change: A CONTACT SHADOW PROMISED IN WRITING MUST BE DECLARED IN THE MARKUP. dossier_check.py now cross-checks the contact-shadow promise: if a slide's dossier names a contact shadow and the slide source exists, its <body> must carry data-contacts with at least one shadow region, and an attribute that is present but empty ([] or entries with no shadow key) fails on its own line so the loophole closes at the same time. One-directional on purpose: data-breather DISABLES a gate and is policed both ways, while data-contacts ENABLES one, so declaring a shadow the dossier never mentioned is a gain and is never flagged. Skipped entirely before the build, so the planning-time run of this gate is unchanged. The failure message carries the full declaration syntax and the alternative remedy, striking the promise.
entries.trigger: Run No.37 deviation, and it is the second clause of the scorer's own one-sentence fix on the criterion that has now been weakest in 8 of 11 runs. All nine dossiers promised a contact shadow in writing; four slides declared one; machine_qa reported NO CONTACTS AT ALL on the other five, and the scorer marked the deck down for bare-plate bands on 03, 05, 06 and 07. qa.py's contact gate is FITTED (known-bad dL 1.24, known-good dL 8.1, FAIL under 4.0) and OPT-IN, so a slide that never writes the attribute is not judged rather than judged clean. Slides 03 and 06 had the two-part shadow DRAWN in their own canvas code and simply never declared it. An opt-in contract is a gate a run can decline, and the run with the most to hide writes the fewest declarations.
entries.verification: RECONSTRUCTION against this run's real artifacts: slides 03, 04, 05, 06 and 07 FAIL, naming exactly the five that promised a shadow and declared none, while 01, 02, 08 and 09 pass. REPAIR PATHS, all three tested on copies: declaring slide 03's comb shadow clears it; data-contacts='[]' on slide 04 fails with 'carries data-contacts with no shadow region in it'; striking the promise from slide 05's dossier clears it. END TO END, the payoff: rendering the repaired slide 03 through UNTOUCHED render.py + qa.py produces a measurement the shipped run never had, "contact shadow: 'the comb block standing on the plate': shadow L* 3.2 vs ground L* 9.4, dL 6.2 at 432w -- under the 8.0 L* comfort band; it reads, barely". BACK CATALOGUE unaffected: runs/*/ carries no slides/ directory so the check is skipped there, and all five re-checked runs still PASS. NOTE: dossier_check now reports FAIL on this run's own out/2026-08-19 artifacts, 5 fails; that is the reconstruction and not a regression, and the deck has shipped.
entries.rollback: revert the upgrade(2026-08-19) commit

entries.change: IF THE RUN DATE IS ALREADY TAKEN, TAKE THE NEXT ONE. Phase 0's date rule now says what to do when a run wakes inside the previous run's date: the run date becomes the first date with no runs/<date>/ directory, the reason goes in run_state.json under date_note, never write into an existing runs/<date>/, never renumber a shipped carousel, and don't ask.
entries.trigger: Run No.37 deviation: America/Anchorage read 2026-08-18 23:15 at wake and runs/2026-08-18/ already held run No.36, because the previous run had taken the same calendar day. Overwriting shipped run artifacts is forbidden by CLAUDE.md, so the showrunner improvised 2026-08-19 and recorded the reasoning. The call was right and nothing in the master prompt told it that. At daily cadence a late-evening wake is a certainty rather than an accident, and improvised correctness is a coin flip repeated nightly. Prose rather than machinery because the decision happens at wake, before any gate exists to hold it; the prohibition was already absolute and what was missing was the answer.
entries.verification: Spec change, no code path. The added text is a restatement of what run No.37 actually did, so it is consistent with the shipped record. House rules checked on it: no em or en dashes, no 'cannot', ordinal date form. No script reads this passage, and the full gate suite was re-run for the other two upgrades with no change in behaviour.

entries.change: AN ART HELPER NOW REFUSES AN OPTION IT DOES NOT KNOW. AK.reliefShade validates its option list, console.errors with an 'AK CONTRACT:' prefix and then THROWS on any unknown key (naming the remedy per key: `mix` -> there is no blend at all, lay the substrate down first or composite a finish yourself with an explicit globalAlpha; `light` -> the option is `lights: [{az,el,w}]`; anything else gets a nearest-key suggestion), and its `low`/`high` ramp is now REQUIRED instead of defaulting to a warm stone. qa.py promotes any console error carrying that prefix from WARN to FAIL, because slide code legitimately wraps art calls in try/catch and a swallowed throw is the same silent no-op. AK.optionContract is exported so other helpers can adopt the same rule.
entries.trigger: Run No.38 deviation 2. Two slides passed `mix: 0.30` / `mix: 0.34` to a function that writes ImageData and REPLACES its region, so a 30 percent form-shading finish was a 100 percent overwrite: slide 05's cold white bond printed as kraft with every printed line on both sheets erased under a gold marker highlighting a blank sheet, and slide 07's bead-blasted anodize printed as a cardboard carton. Nine pixel critics scored the round at a mean of 4.28 while machine QA was WARN with zero fails. Found during this retro and not previously recorded: the SHIPPED deck still passes `mix: 0.20` on slide 07 and `light: [x,y,z]` on both, so three silently ignored options survived four revision rounds, every gate and the merge.
entries.verification: Reconstruction A (this run's exact shape: mix + light inside the author's own try/catch) renders OK and qa.py FAILS it with 'library contract: AK CONTRACT: AK.reliefShade: unknown options `light` ... `mix` ...'. Reconstruction B (ramp unset, throw uncaught) is a render.py HARD FAIL. The control slide (correct call) renders clean at 0 fails 0 warns. Re-rendering the SHIPPED nine slides now FAILS exactly slides 05 and 07, on the real defect they carry, with the other seven at 0/0; note the refusal also removes their relief, which drops slide 05's declared encoding to dE 1.9 and fails the encoding gate too, i.e. the deck can't ship until the call is corrected. examples/demo-deck is identical before and after (WARN, 0 fails, 11 warns).

entries.change: THE PLAN AND THE BUILD NOW HAVE TO AGREE ABOUT THE BUILD. New scripts/plan_drift_check.py cross-checks the storyboard's claims index against copy.json's per-slide claim_ids in BOTH directions (a claim marked NOT USED must appear on no slide; an unknown-shaped index or a copy.json with no claim_ids at all is CANNOT LOOK, exit 2, like copy_sync_check's zero-strings rule), and checks every '<N> declared marks / leaders / measured axes / encodings / contact shadows' sentence in a dossier against what the slide body actually declares in the render report. Claim tags printed in the render are reported as evidence of which artifact drifted, never as a source of pass or fail. New gate_status.py row `plan_drift` and step 7 of Phase 8.
entries.trigger: Run No.38 deviation 3: plan-versus-pixel drift was flagged by the scorer in all three scoring rounds and was the one defect class the run never got ahead of (claim ids assigned to slides that never printed them, a dossier still saying five marks after three shipped, aggregates.json quoting a mono note the render had stopped printing). Each was caught by a human-equivalent reader, never by a gate. The storyboard that SHIPPED still over-assigns C03, C07, C10 and C24 and still says FIVE declared marks and TWO DECLARED MEASURED AXES against three and one in the build.
entries.verification: `python scripts/plan_drift_check.py --self-test` passes 11 hermetic checks, including both No.38 defect shapes as reconstructions (an id indexed to a slide copy.json does not carry FAILS; 'FIVE declared marks' against 3 in the build FAILS) and the set-aliasing bug found while building it (one row's slide set was shared by every claim on that row, which reported 33 drifts on runs/2026-08-09, none of them real). On out/2026-08-20 it reports all seven real drifts and exits 1; the gate_status row renders FAIL with the first drift named and gate_status --self-test still passes 16 checks. Swept over all 27 shipped runs carrying both artifacts: 1 to 10 drifts each on the 11 that have claim_ids, CANNOT LOOK on the rest, and the three sampled by hand (2026-08-06, 08-09, 08-19) were true positives verified against the artifacts.

entries.change: SCREEN-SPACE ANNOTATION IS DERIVED FROM THE CAMERA, NEVER TYPED. New AKT.screenBox(R, meshOrGroupOrArray, {pad,padX,padY,w,h}) returns {x,y,w,h,cx,cy,rx,ry,corners,behind,offscreen} in DESIGN px, computed from each mesh's OWN local bounding box through its matrixWorld and the live camera (tighter than a world-space Box3, which axis-aligns before projecting), plus AKT.projectPoint for a leader terminus. `behind` and `offscreen` console.error under the AK CONTRACT prefix, which qa.py now FAILs, because both states return a reasonable-looking rectangle that encloses nothing.
entries.trigger: Run No.38 deviation 1, the run's dominant defect shape: slide 06's four dashed gold origin contours, the deck's central accuracy device, were HARDCODED SCREEN ELLIPSES while the parts they name were placed by a 3D camera, so every contour enclosed bare foam. Nine pixel critics returned a mean of 4.28 and machine QA was WARN with zero fails. The in-run repair was written inline in the slide; this commits it once so the next slide reaches for it instead of typing coordinates.
entries.verification: Measured against pixels, not asserted: a rotated 1.2x0.6x0.9 box at a known pose reported BOX 361.2 522.0 370.6 322.2 in design px, and the object's ink bbox measured off the rendered PNG is 361.0 522.0 371.0 322.5 -- inside half a design pixel on every edge. Aiming the camera away from the part produces the AK CONTRACT console error and a qa.py FAIL ('the target is partly BEHIND the camera') instead of a plausible box. examples/demo-deck and this run's nine slides re-render with no change attributable to this addition (it adds functions only).

entries.change: TYPE NOBODY SIZED IS NOW A HARD FAIL. render.py records, per text element, whether ANY author font-size applies anywhere on its ancestor chain (an inline style, which is what AK.fitText writes; an SVG presentation attribute; or a matching rule in any readable stylesheet, walked through @media and @supports), and qa.py FAILs a non-decorative text element when none does, because the size then came from Chromium's user-agent stylesheet and the 16px initial value alone. Not opt-in and nothing to tune: the author's own file states no size. A slide with an unreadable stylesheet is counted (render_report css_unreadable) and demotes the finding to a WARN naming which half of the check went blind, so it can't false-fail on a rule it could not read.
entries.trigger: Run No.39 deviation 1, the run's most expensive catch. slide-07.html styled its <h2> headline with position, left, top, width, family, weight, variation settings, line-height, tracking and colour and NO font-size, and never loaded assets/js/aktype.js, so AK.fitText was never called and the deck's hook line typeset at 1.5em of an unstyled 16px root: 24px, the size of the mono labels beside it, 9.6px at the 432px feed width. entries.change: DECLARED ARTWORK NOW HAS TO REACH THE SLIDE. A slide names the drawn features that carry meaning, window.__akMotifs = [{what, rect:[x,y,w,h]}] in design px; render.py reads that rect back out of the canvas the motif was drawn on and takes an elementsFromPoint census of what stands on it, and qa.py samples the same rect out of the composited PNG. FAILS when 15 percent or less of the rect is clear of opaque DOM, when the rect is one flat colour in the render, or when under 25 percent of the ink the canvas holds survives to the page. Opt-in like every other declaration contract, so a slide that declares nothing is not judged, and every FAIL is the slide contradicting itself. Two calibration facts are in the code: the ink statistic is the mean of the top 1 percent of dE from the region's own median (p95 reads a 1.5px rule in a 920x20 band as ABSENT at 2.9 dE while p99 finds it at 58.7), and the page side is read at full resolution with an integer stride rather than through a smoothing resize, which would cost a thin mark 40 percent of its spread and put a visible motif within a point of the survival floor.

entries.change: The contact-shadow probe now says WHERE THE CAST ACTUALLY IS. When a declared shadow fails or warns, qa.py measures the row-lightness profile over the object's own x span inside a bounded window, finds the band of dark rows NEAREST the declaration (reported as its dark core, since a soft cast fades for tens of pixels), and prints it beside the declared band when the two do not overlap. No threshold moved: CONTACT_FAIL_DL 4.0 and CONTACT_WARN_DL 8.0 decide the verdict exactly as before and the new text is appended to a verdict already made.
entries.trigger: Run No.44 spent two of its three revision rounds on this ambiguity. Slides 02, 04 and 07 declared shadow bands their cast never reached (S04 declared y 728-748 while the cast ran 714-726), so the probe sampled lit glass and reported dL 4.6 to 5.9, 'it reads, barely'. The natural reading of that warn is 'make the shadow darker', which is the wrong fix and the one the run tried first: it put machine ink on a near-black ground at 1.8:1 and crossed the axis numerals, then over-corrected to dL 70, which the scorer called a black bar. It also works the standing repeat offender: artwork craft has been the weakest criterion in 8 of the last 10 scored runs (mean 6.75) and 'warns:contact shadow' is on trend_check's still-shipping list with its latest occurrence in this very run.
entries.verification: Reconstructed on this run's own pixels. Slide 08's declaration is CORRECT and stays silent (dL 7.5 warn, no diagnosis). Shifted 16, 24 and 40 px off its cast it reports 'the nearest band of dark rows over this object's own x span is y 1118-1140 (L* 74.9, dL 10.2 against the same ground) while the declaration points at y 1144-1160'. Slide 06 shifted +22 and -18 px finds its true cast core at y 718-735 against a cast drawn at 714-730. Zero diagnoses fire across the nine shipped slides and the per-slide fail/warn counts match runs/2026-08-29/machine_qa.json exactly. The first cut took the DARKEST run and mis-diagnosed slide 08's correct declaration by pointing at the pencil itself (L* 56.9 at y 1086-1105); an object is darker than its own shadow, which is why the shipped rule is nearest-and-not-overlapping with a dark-core reduction. demo-deck declares no contacts and is unaffected.

entries.change: render.py now exports the CANVAS LAYER on its own (slide-NN.canvas.png: every visible canvas re-composited at design size with nothing from the DOM on top), and qa.py FAILS a canvas mark that has broken into a reserved text block -- a text block of two or more lines whose OTHER lines sit on clean paper, one of which carries a hard-edged local mark. Measured on the canvas alone and in the densest 40px window rather than over the whole line box.
entries.trigger: Two hard fails in one run, both found by the scorer AFTER qa.py reported 9/9 PASS with 0 fails and 0 warns on the same renders: slide 04 drew a registration crosshair on top of the display headline and slide 08 drew twelve register ticks through the last line of the body copy (storyboard.md, ROUND 4). The gap is structural, not a loose threshold. text_collisions() is DOM-vs-DOM by construction; busy_art_under_text() and glyph_ink_contamination() do read canvas ink but read the COMPOSITED png, so both must mask the glyph ink off first and both then average over a whole line box, which dilutes a local mark on a long line to nothing -- measured on the reconstruction, the crosshair scored a background edge density of 0.003 against a 0.03 warn line. The discriminator that needs no taste is the slide's own layout: a block whose sibling lines are clean paper has demonstrated that its author reserved that paper, while a single-line label floating on a map has no sibling to prove intent, so the check abstains there and leaves it to the pixel critics. Design bar taken from the frontier scan (Google Tricorder, abseil.io SWE-book ch.20): on-by-default checks must sit under 10 percent effective false positives and must say how to fix what they find.
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION: rebuilt both round-3 states from the shipped sources (slide 04 regCross moved from the margin at (958,176) to (520,226) on the headline; slide 08 SEAMY 1108 -> 1075 so the ticks re-cross the body's last line), rendered, and confirmed by eye on the crop that the crosshair sits on the word 'means'. The pre-change qa.py raises NO fail and NO warn on either. The post-change qa.py FAILS both, naming the line and its coordinates: slide 04 line 1 of 2 at (80,172), 378 px^2, densest window 22.7%; slide 08 line 6 of 6 at (80,1026), 213 px^2, densest window 6.5%. NEGATIVE CONTROL: calibrated on 122 multi-line boxes across this run's 9 shipped slides and the 4 demo-deck slides; the worst clean box scores 83 px^2 / 2.9% and misses BOTH conditions (thresholds 150 px^2 and 4.5%), so 0 false positives on the corpus. Before/after diff of machine_qa.json on both decks against the pre-change qa.py: this run's slides PASS 0 fails 0 warns before and after (matching the run's own recorded result), demo-deck WARN 0 fails 11 warns before and after -- no new fail, no new warn, and no fail or warn LOST. Full re-render + qa after all three upgrades: this run's slides 9/9 OK then PASS; demo-deck 4/4 OK then WARN 11, unchanged. Abstain paths tested individually and each announces itself as a warn rather than passing silently: a report predating the export, a layer marked approximate (CSS transform/filter/blend), and a missing layer file.

entries.trigger: d3's fitExtent and fitSize PRESERVE ASPECT and fit the SMALLER dimension, so asking for a full-width band with .fitExtent([[110,0],[980,1]], mainland) renders a sliver and returns success. Run No.45's slide 08 did exactly that and rendered 27px of a declared full-width grazing seam; it cost a hard fail and a whole review round, and no gate could see it because the render is not blank, the projection is valid and nothing is thrown. Instinct fitextent-fits-the-smaller-dimension, confidence 0.99. The run's own repair rescaled the OUTPUT coordinates by hand afterwards, which leaves the projection and the drawing disagreeing about where things are.
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION: put the round-3 call back into slide 08 verbatim. render.py prints '[projection] slide-08.html: fitExtent box 870.0x1.0 line 128' and qa.py FAILS with the remedy named. Only fully LITERAL boxes are read, so a box built from variables is never guessed at -- false negatives traded for the certainty that a hit is real. fitAxis VERIFIED NUMERICALLY in a real browser against the actual mainland collection: fitAxis(...,[110,980],'x') gives an x span of 870.00 starting at x=110.00; with {at:1108} the y centre lands at 1108.00; fitAxis(...,[200,700],'y') gives a y span of 500.00 starting at y=200.00; the raw d3 call it replaces gives 1.45 x 1.00, which is the trap, measured.

entries.change: NEW scripts/value_structure.py, measures a slide's value structure, the notan, off the rendered pixels. Reads at qa.py's own 432px feed width in qa.py's own CIELAB L*, clusters into three masses with seeded 1D k-means so a dark deck and a light deck are each judged against their own values, then checks four craft rules: one mass over half the frame, the two lesser masses deliberately unequal, the darks welded into one shape after a SQUINT pass, and the dominant mass actually reaching the bottom third.
entries.trigger: Artwork craft has been the weakest scored criterion in 9 of the last 10 runs at a mean of 6.65 while every other criterion sat above 8, and the two defects that keep shipping inside a green machine_qa, busy art under text and top-loaded composition, are one problem seen twice. Nothing in the repo could see it, because every existing check reads the thumb for LEGIBILITY and none reads it for STRUCTURE. Craft refresh of 2026-08-31, https://www.virtualartacademy.com/notan/
entries.verification: Calibrated on two known-good decks in opposite value registers before use. The first version counted connected components on raw dark pixels and flagged 9 of 9 slides on runs/2026-08-30, a deck that scored 8.79 with its best artwork craft mark in ten runs, which is a 100 percent false positive rate. Adding the squint pass, a box blur and re-threshold before counting, took it to 1 of 9 there and 3 of 4 on examples/demo-deck, and both remaining flags point at something real. 2 flags across 13 known-good frames, about 15 percent, which is close to the Tricorder bar for a default-on check and not under it. That is why it REPORTS and is deliberately NOT wired into gate_status.py. This run's own deck measures 9 of 9 holding.

entries.trigger: Run No.47's slide 07 solved nine analytic shadow tips and drew NONE of them. A clip test asked whether each cast point was left of a surveyed cut and broke at s=0 for every marker, so every wedge was built base to base and filled at zero length, and the slide's declared focal point was never in the picture. The compositional root cause was that the boundary descended in the same bearing the sun throws shadows, so it overtook its own shadows within ten pixels of the marker bases. render.py, qa.py, dossier_check and bespoke_check all passed it; a pixel critic caught it one full review round after it shipped into the first render. Same family as the 2026-08-25 buried motif and the 2026-08-31 clipped marks, but one question earlier: those two ask whether declared ink SURVIVED, and nothing was asking whether the canvas ever had anything to survive.
entries.verification: CALIBRATED BEFORE IT WAS WIRED IN, on 22 known-good slides from three decks (out/2026-09-01, runs/2026-08-31, examples/demo-deck): 10,999 fill() calls at 155 call sites carrying exactly ONE degenerate fill anywhere, ak3d.js's triangle rasteriser at 1 of 9,216 at that site. That is a ratio of 0.0001 against the 0.8 the gate needs and a count of 1 against the 3, so both thresholds clear the corpus by orders of magnitude. THE REAL DEFECT RECONSTRUCTED, on the shipped slide itself: restore the s=0 break in out/2026-09-01/slides/slide-07.html (ex=x, ey=base) and qa.py FAILS with exactly one message, '9 of 9 fills at slide-07.html:223:68 enclosed no area (last one measured 31.75 x 0 px)', where the unmodified slide is silent across all 364 of its fills. entries.change: assemble.py records the sha256 of every render PNG and slide HTML it consumed into assemble_report.json, and gate_status's `assemble` row re-hashes them and FAILS when any input changed, was deleted or appeared since the build, so deliverables made from a superseded render are a hard fail instead of a green gate.
entries.trigger: Run No.48 edited slide 03 during a fix round, re-ran render.py, and never re-ran assemble.py. The shipped 432 px thumb and the full-size PNG therefore came from two different builds, as did the contact sheet the flow critic read and the PDF. A pixel critic caught it by transcribing both. No gate could see it: assemble_report.json recorded the PDF bytes, the mode, the slide count and the thumb paths, and nothing at all about WHICH renders the build was made from, so the divergence was not expressible as arithmetic. Same family as the 2026-08-14 stale-render hash check, which asks whether a PNG matches its HTML, one step downstream: nothing asked whether the DELIVERABLES matched the PNGs. mtimes are deliberately not the test, because a checkout or a copy rewrites them and proves nothing.

entries.change: launch_chromium PROBES a candidate browser's ability to fetch() a committed asset over file:// and rejects one that cannot, instead of inferring the capability from the binary's path, and it now also knows the Chrome for Testing directory layouts.
entries.trigger: https://playwright.dev/docs/release-notes -- Playwright 1.57 stopped shipping Chromium and now manages Chrome for Testing, headed as `chrome` and headless as `chrome-headless-shell`. The 2026-08-27 fix answered the same hazard by ORDERING the candidate list full-binary-first, which is right and is not enough: this repo finds its browser with a /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-*/chrome-linux/chrome glob, and when a container refresh moves the binaries out from under that glob the ordering has nothing left to order and the fallback returns the default channel, which since 1.57 is the shell. The shell cannot read the disk, the SKILL contract documents fetch('@@ASSETS@@/geo/...') as the way a slide gets a map, and the failure is SILENT: the browser launches, the page loads, every gate is green, and only the geodata is gone. This repo already lost examples/demo-deck to exactly that on run No.42. A capability is now established by testing it.
entries.verification: BOTH HALVES MEASURED ON THIS MACHINE, same flags, same target file. /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome (141.0.7390.37) fetches assets/geo/alaska-state.geo.json over file:// and returns ok; /opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1194/chrome-linux/headless_shell, the SAME Chromium version, returns 'fetch blocked: Failed to fetch'. tests/chromium_fileread_verify.py asserts the control, the defect and the wiring (launch_chromium returns a browser that passes the probe) and exits 0. End to end after the change: examples/demo-deck renders 4/4 OK with 0 errors and qa.py is byte-for-byte the same verdict as before, WARN 0 fails / 11 warns, and assembles to a 7.31 MB vector PDF. Cost is one extra page load per render invocation, about 200 ms, once. If NOTHING passes the probe the first launchable browser is used anyway with a loud stderr warning, so this can never turn a renderable run into a dead one.

entries.trigger: Run No.49 produced the same artwork defect four times from one cause (slides 01, 06, 08, 09: a tangled ribbon on a fluted pole, a topographic map on a road, marbled endpaper on enamel) and diagnosed it four separate times. entries.trigger: Run No.50's slide 08 lit 31 of 72 grid cells to stand for 31 sections of two townships whose location is not published, under a label reading EXTENT ONLY. NO BOUNDARY IS DRAWN. The build shuffled the 72 cells and took the first 31; they landed edge to edge in one township and the frame drew a solid parcel with holes in it, seventy pixels under that label. __akAssert counted 31 of 31 and the 2026-08-31 pixel probe found all 31 painted, and both were RIGHT: the count contract asks how many and the erasure contract asks whether they painted, and this defect is about where. Artwork craft is also the standing repeat offender in scripts/trend_check.py, weakest in 8 of the last 10 runs at a mean of 6.7, and this is that criterion's most expensive failure mode: a picture that argues something the data does not support.
entries.verification: CALIBRATED BEFORE IT WAS WIRED IN, on 4,000 simulated uniform-random scatters per count over four field aspect ratios. The largest touching mass under chance runs: n=12 median 0.33 p99 0.75; n=20 median 0.20 p99 0.55; n=31 median 0.16 p99 0.39; n=50 median 0.12 p99 0.28. P(mass >= 0.75) is 0.011 at n=12, 0.003 at n=16 and 0.000 at n>=20, so the 0.75 line sits past the 99th percentile of chance everywhere it speaks, and below 12 marks it declines to speak at all. Run No.50's own two real cohorts: the shipped repaired set measures 0.06 (2 of 31), the defect measures 1.00 (31 of 31), a factor of 1.3 clear of the line. The link multiplier is the middle of a plateau, 1.05 to 1.35 give the identical answer on a lattice, above sqrt(2) everything connects. FAIL-FIRST RECONSTRUCTION, committed as tests/mark_spread_verify.py: four fixtures lighting 31 of the same 72 cells through the real render.py and qa.py. The defect (one solid township) FAILS at 100 percent; the shipped connectivity-capped build holds at 10 percent; a plain seeded shuffle, the build the run rejected by eye, holds at 32 percent, so the gate does not fire on chance; and the same defect cells with the flag left off are silent, because the check is opt-in. entries.change: qa.py WARNs when a declared contact shadow and the ground it is measured against are more than CONTACT_PAIR_SPAN (96 design px) apart. There is still deliberately NO upper bound on dL, because a deep shadow is not a defect; the check is on the GEOMETRY of the declaration, since a pair that reaches across the picture is measuring the scene's own lighting falloff or a second surface and dL can't tell you which. The message names the measured gap, the window, and the fix that is nearly always right (widen the lit pool, never widen the reach), and it never lowers a verdict: a fail stays a fail with the sentence appended.
entries.trigger: Run No.52 passed two declared contact shadows through qa.py that were not measuring a shadow at all. Slide 08's declared rect sat on the camera's own dark mount plate and read dL 55; slide 04's pair straddled 115 design px of open sediment and read dL 25, which was the strobe's falloff across the frame. Both returned INFO and printed nothing; five pixel critics found them by looking, and repairing them cost rounds under the five-round cap. The physical cause was identical twice: the occlusion pool was drawn no wider than the object, so the object covered all of it and there was no lit ground beside the foot to pair against.
entries.verification: CALIBRATED, not guessed. entries.change: qa.py's axis census now says WHICH declared mark is dead and where its ink actually is, instead of reporting the minimum and throwing the rest away. When some declared marks carry mark-strength ink and others sit at the band's noise floor, it prints the per-mark ink table, states that this is not a drawing-weight problem, searches up to 200 design px for the nearest position that does carry mark-strength ink, prints that position and the value it reads as, and names the cause a constant offset almost always has: a scale corrected in data-scale and left alone in the code that DRAWS it. Strictly a message change; it can only re-route a warn that already fired, never invent one.
entries.trigger: Run No.52's slide 07 had its data-scale endpoint corrected from x 1000 to x 960 while the canvas variable that draws the axis stayed at 1000, so two of three declared marks had no ink under them at all. The census caught it and said 'the weakest declared mark is no stronger than the band's own texture ... draw the marks so a reader can tell them from the ground', which describes a stroke-weight problem, and the run spent a round on stroke weights. Shaped by the measured result in https://arxiv.org/html/2607.14167v1 : in a 50-game repair study, feedback carrying failure location plus observed value alone performed close to a raw validator error, and it was the ADMISSIBLE ALTERNATIVE that moved repair success 36 to 40 points (28 to 72 percent on Qwen2.5-Coder-14B, 16 to 58 on Llama-3.1-8B).
entries.verification: DEFECT RECONSTRUCTION on this run's own slide 07 render, declaring the marks on the un-drawn 1000 scale (620, 715, 1000) against a band drawn on the 960 one. Old code: 'the weakest declared mark (ink 0.9) is no stronger than the band's own texture (0.8) ... draw the marks so a reader can tell them from the ground'. New code, same input, same WARN verdict: '1 of this axis's 3 declared mark(s) carry no more ink than the band's own texture (0.8), while the strongest declared mark reads 50.1. Per mark: 620 (0 kilometres): ink 50.1, 715 (50 kilometres): ink 8.1, 1000 (200 kilometres): ink 0.9. ... The nearest mark-strength ink to the mark declared at 1000 is at 961, 39 px away'. NO NEW WARNS BY CONSTRUCTION: the new branch is reachable only when min(declared_ink) is at or below max(0.5, floor*1.2), which is exactly the condition the two pre-existing warn branches already tripped on, so no census that used to pass can now warn. entries.change: dossier_check.py cross-checks every FIGURE in a dossier's COPY block against claims.json before the art is built. A number in quoted copy must appear in some claim's claim/value/verbatim; a number that appears only in a claim's NOTES fails by name as reasoning rather than verification; a number that appears nowhere fails as unsourced. Out of scope, all by shape rather than by exception: rails, counters and kickers by their bullet label, progress counters and font-axis strings, and CITATIONS AND IDENTIFIERS on both sides of the comparison (43 U.S.C. 1606(i), 18 CFR 385, 91 FR 55826, Public Law 92-203, WC 26-173, P-15423-000, a PIID, a notice id), which are addresses rather than measurements. A number that belongs to the drawing rather than the world is declared [design] on its bullet.
entries.trigger: Run No.53 planned and printed '102 SIGNATURES' plus a 102-mark struck field on the strength of a scout paragraph the first claims pass never turned into a claim and never killed. claims_check, aggregate_check and plan_drift all passed, because each checks the claims that EXIST rather than the figures a dossier quotes. It was found by reading during the Phase 8 pixel rounds, and verifying it late also corrected it three ways, at the cost of a re-render. The same run printed '1971' twice in mono for four scoring rounds where C35 verifies only 'at incorporation' and the year lived only in a note as 'consistent with 1971'; that capped round 3 and was probably wrong, since ANCSA was signed in 1971 and the regional corporations incorporated in 1972. brand.yaml has required a claim-id on every on-slide number since the beginning and nothing enforced it.
entries.verification: tests/figure_backing_verify.py HOLDS over six fixtures: the 102 line with no claim FAILs, the same line once C54 exists passes, the 1971 line FAILs and names C35 and the NOTES field, the same line printing what C35 verifies passes, a drawing constant marked [design] passes, and a rail plus a progress counter pass. Measured on this run's own storyboard it returns four findings, all real: the round-5 removal '2019 JOINT ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CENTER' (the JAIC-named contract in the record is a 2020 one), the round-3 capping defect 1971, a statute citation printed from a note, and '$632,119.41' -- a subtraction on the deck's most legally sensitive sentence that no claim carries and that aggregate_check's shape detector never saw. Calibrated across fourteen shipped storyboards: 0 to 6 findings each, median 3, and the residue is dominated by printed art-provenance slugs (a synthetic-sun azimuth, a depth, a scale key) which are one [design] tag each. Exemptions were fitted, not guessed: matching the furniture word anywhere in the bullet's label cut a 17-finding deck to 4, and the counter and font-axis shape rules took the noisiest deck from 17 to 4. AND ONE FALSE POSITIVE, FOUND BY THE SHOWRUNNER ON FIRST USE AND FIXED THE SAME HOUR: '43 U.S.C. 1606(i)' was read as the figures 43 and 1606, on a line whose claim C31 was read at uscode.house.gov and whose subject IS that citation. Citation shapes are now blanked out of the copy AND out of the claims, the second so that a claim which merely mentions a statute cannot make a bare 1606 a verified figure elsewhere. Re-measured over the same fifteen storyboards: 36 findings before, 34 after, and a line-by-line diff shows the ONLY change is the two copies of the citation hit (out/2026-09-07 and runs/2026-09-07), with nothing added. Two shapes were added because the claims-side strip exposed them on runs/2026-08-31, whose slides print '91 FR 55826' and the FCC docket 'WC 26-173': with those in, that deck is back to its original findings exactly. tests/figure_backing_verify.py now HOLDS over eight fixtures, the two new ones being the statute cite beside a figure C31 verifies (clean) and a bare '1606 SHAREHOLDERS' beside the same cite (FAILS, because the cite backs nothing).

entries.change: render.py watches the canvas PATH, not only the pixels it produced. A new CLIP_RULE_HOOK_JS tracks per-subpath bounding boxes in device space and records two things: a path that was BUILT and then discarded by beginPath() with nothing painted from it, and every even-odd clip()/fill() with a census of its subpaths. qa.py FAILS a discarded path that contained a FULL-FRAME subpath (the attached-cast idiom losing its outer rect) and WARNs on any other unpainted discard; it WARNs, with both rects and the destination-out repair printed, when two AXIS-ALIGNED RECT reserves of one even-odd operation overlap. The outer shape of a reserve is excluded by AREA rather than by full-frame-ness, which is what keeps the overlap test silent on region-scoped reserves. The hook only observes and forwards; the current transform is cached per context and invalidated by the eight calls that can change it, and a stack is taken only once a record is going to be written.
entries.trigger: Run No.54 refactored the cockled sheet outline of four slides onto a shared sheetPath() that opened with cx.beginPath(). Canvas discards the current path there, so the idiom beginPath(); rect(0,0,W,H); <outline>; clip('evenodd') lost its full-frame rect, the clip became the sheet rather than everything-but-the-sheet, and the cast shadows of slides 02, 03, 04 and 08 were drawn INSIDE their own sheets where the sheet's fill hid them. Four slides lost their contacts in one commit and every render looked plausible, because a missing shadow is an absence and not an artefact; only qa.py's contact gate caught it, and only on the two slides whose declared rects happened to sample the right band. The same run reserved type on slide 02 by adding one rect per element to an even-odd clip, two of the elements overlapped by 25px, and a region covered by the outer shape plus two rects has three crossings, which is odd, which is inside again, so the set lines painted back into the reserve exactly where the two elements touched and read as a broken glyph at the slide's own declared focal point. qa.py called that one 'busy art under text', which is the right flag with the wrong cause and would never have led anyone to destination-out.
entries.verification: tests/clip_reserve_verify.py HOLDS over four fixtures, two pairs each broken and repaired: the cast drawn through a helper that opens its own path FAILS and names both the site that built the path and the helper that discarded it, the same helper contributing a subpath is clean, two reserved boxes overlapping by 30px WARN and the message names (150,640) 620x96 and (170,706) 560x96, and the same two elements reserved as one box is clean. Both clean fixtures build a full-frame even-odd reserve and clip through it, so neither check fires on the idiom itself. FITTED, NOT GUESSED, over 32 shipped slides re-rendered through the hook (out/2026-09-09 ten, examples/demo-deck four, runs/2026-09-07 nine, runs/2026-09-05 nine): 62 even-odd operations, ZERO discards of any kind, and the overlap instrument fires only on run No.53, whose clipOut() helper punches six to ten padded rects out of a frame rect on five slides. Those are not false positives. On its slide 03 two of the four reported pairs are real element overlaps, 164x26 and 164x14 design px of unreserved paper between two type blocks, and two are 6px slivers where only the 8px inflation touches. There is no gap between those populations to put a threshold in, which is exactly why the overlap verdict is a WARN and the discard verdict is a FAIL. THE HOOK CHANGES NOTHING IT WATCHES: all 14 slides of out/2026-09-09 and examples/demo-deck re-render byte-identical to their pre-change baselines (sha256 per PNG), render times are unchanged within noise, and qa.py's output on both decks is line-for-line identical at 0 fails and 11 warns each. It is installed BEFORE the paint hook on purpose: the paint hook reads its call site off stack frame 2, and putting this one outside it collapsed 3 call sites to 1 and broke tests/empty_paint_verify.py. All 21 tests/*_verify.py HOLD.

entries.change: A COLOUR LAW IS NOW A CHECKED DECLARATION. Each frame may declare its law-bearing inks on <body data-ink> as [{hex, means, state:"present"|"absent"}]; render.py keeps a per-frame INK CENSUS of every colour a brush actually carried (canvas fill, stroke and canvas text, gradient stops resolved through addColorStop, DOM text nodes, SVG shapes), keyed on the rgb triple with the highest effective alpha; and qa.py FAILS a forbidden ink any brush used, a promised ink no brush used, and a promised ink that reached the render as ZERO pixels of its hue family, with a WARN under a fitted thinness floor and for an ink within 2 to 5 dE of a forbidden one. dossier_check.py now parses data-ink before any render is spent, and a frame that declares no law while others do gets a WARN.
entries.trigger: This run's headline finding, in knowledge/FIELD_NOTES.md and ledger/instincts.json: the deck's whole argument was that #FFC72C is what the record knows and #7D8F94 is what it does not, the first build broke it in three places, and claims, dossier, aggregate, plan-drift, copy-sync and machine QA all passed it at zero fails and zero warns.
