entries.verification: The instrument was CHOSEN by measurement, not assumed. Pixels-only, the gate the instinct proposed, was built and rejected first: gold rays put back on slides 01 and 08 changed 81k and 242k pixels and moved the count of gold-hued pixels by zero, because gold at alpha 0.34 over cool ice composites to a desaturated green ([70,142,155] to [81,136,125]); and frames that never used #7D8F94 carry 1,727 to 40,027 pixels within dE 4 of it. Hence brush for the forbidden half, pixels for the promised half. FIT, known good: this run's eight renderable shipped frames with the deck's real law declared (gold present on all, #3CE6B4 absent except 04, #7D8F94 absent on 02 and 04) pass at 0 fails and 0 warns. FIT, known bad, both reconstructions rendered: the provenance mark set in #7D8F94 on slide 02 FAILS with the op named ('dom-text rgb(125, 143, 148) x1 at alpha 1.00'); slide 03's gold ticks as a degenerate subpath FAIL with 'painted by 8 op(s) and reached the frame as ZERO pixels'; the sub-pixel 0.75 degree arc variant WARNS at 33 native px^2, '1.3 px^2 in a 432px thumb'. Tolerance was fitted the same way: dE 8 hard-failed two CORRECT frames because #8FA3A8 sits 7.49 dE from #7D8F94, so it is 2.0 with a 2-to-5 warn band. Thinness floor 120 native px^2 sits at half the weakest gold-bearing shipped frame (236) and twice the no-warm-ink noise floor (15 to 60 across three earlier decks). Regression: examples/demo-deck renders clean and qa.py reports 0 fails with no ink-law line on any slide, and every deck before today declares nothing and is judged on nothing. Cost measured: render +52ms on the 9,216-stroke demo slide (861 vs 809ms), qa.py +1.3s per declared frame in float32 (the f64 path cost 3.4s and the two Lab arrays agree to 7e-5). entries.change: scripts/unbound_names_check.py, a new check that walks each Python file's AST and reports every module-scope name the file LOADS that nothing in the module BINDS. Conservative by construction, because a false alarm would train people to ignore it: a star import, or any call to globals, locals, vars, exec or eval, disables the file entirely, and a name bound anywhere in the module counts as bound everywhere. Exit 0 clean, 1 on a finding. Covers scripts/ and the carousel engine by default.
entries.trigger: The fix above, generalised. Python resolves module-scope names at RUN time, so an unbound name imports, compiles and passes every other gate; the only way to find it is to take the branch that reads it. This machine is mostly gates, most of their branches are rare BY DESIGN because they fire on defects, and a rare branch is exactly where an unbound name hides. Informed by this run's Phase 12 frontier scan on self-improving pipeline patterns, whose most useful finding was the same shape, a project staging every projection and reporting module-scope names nothing in the staged set binds, kept as a ratchet.
entries.verification: The defect reconstructs. Run against a copy of qa.py with MARK_PROBE_MAX removed, the check reports the exact line and exits 1. Run against the repaired tree it passes 49 files at exit 0, so it is not crying wolf across the existing machine. It was also run against a path outside the repo, which crashed the first draft on relative_to and is now handled.

entries.change: A MATERIAL FLAG THE SHADER MAY NEVER HAVE BEEN TOLD ABOUT. render.py gains scan_material_flags(): a recompile-triggering three.js material property (vertexColors, flatShading, fog, the map slots, alphaTest, blending, premultipliedAlpha, combine) assigned as a STATEMENT after the material was built, with no needsUpdate on the same receiver later in the same file, is recorded per slide; qa.py raises a WARN for each one. It reads inline scripts AND the house libraries the slide loads (assets/js/ak*.js), because the pattern lives in a shared chassis, and skips vendored libraries. Narrowed to receivers whose last identifier segment looks like a material, so scene.fog and an options object's map are never judged; the constructor's object-literal form has no '=' and can never match. SHIPPED AS A FAIL AND DOWNGRADED TO A WARN THE SAME DAY, on measurement: see the trigger.
entries.trigger: Run No.61 set mat.vertexColors = true on a built clay material in assets/js/akdrift.js and never set needsUpdate, and the run believed that was why every deposit rendered white for a revision round. CORRECTION, measured 2026-09-17 after a Codex review challenged the premise: it was not. Deleting the needsUpdate line and re-rendering slides 01, 06, 07 and 09 gives a max per-pixel difference of 0 on all four. three.js compiles a material's program at FIRST RENDER, so a flag set between construction and first render needs no needsUpdate. The white drift had another cause. The scanner therefore matches the common CORRECT sequence, cannot decide from source whether an assignment precedes first render, and must not be a FAIL: a FAIL on an undecidable question blocks correct decks. It is a WARN for the real case it does catch, a flag set on a material that has already been drawn.
entries.verification: Corpus: scan_material_flags over the 49 slides on disk (out/2026-09-17, examples/demo-deck, runs/2026-09-1x) finds 1 assignment, akdrift.js, correctly paired with its needsUpdate, and reports 0 hits. Pipeline: render.py + qa.py on out/2026-09-17/slides -> 9/9 OK, 0 page errors, verdict PASS, 0 fails, 0 warns. RECONSTRUCTION, re-measured 2026-09-17 after the FAIL was downgraded to a WARN: with 'mat.needsUpdate = true;' deleted from assets/js/akdrift.js, render prints '[material] slide-01.html: mat.vertexColors at assets/js/akdrift.js:614 with no needsUpdate' and qa.py returns fails=0 warns=1 on that slide. The earlier record here claimed FAIL, fails=1, which was true of the gate as first shipped and is no longer true; a verification field that describes a superseded implementation is worse than none. entries.change: aggregate_check.py gained a SUBSET detector and a `subset` declaration kind: a slide string that counts a subset of a claim's enumerated list ("nine of the ten", "all but one of the six", "every one of the ten", "none of the eight") must now name WHICH members of that enumeration it means, and the gate parses the enumeration out of the claim's own verbatim so the printed total is re-derived from the source rather than trusted. Route A (the claim enumerates) takes 1-based `selected` indices plus the `terms` that separate the subset from the remainder, and the terms must PARTITION: every selected item has to match one and no unselected item may match any. Route B (the set is real but nothing enumerates it, "TWO OF 32 PRECINCTS") takes a `basis` note and requires both printed figures to be standalone figures in the claim's claim/value/verbatim, with "(1)".."(10)" markers blanked first because an item index is an address and not a quantity. `from_claim` and `design` can no longer swallow a subset detection, which is a tightening. CODEX ROUND (PR #391, head 31e9ef7) closed eight holes in that first cut, all real: (1) n > total is now a FAILING subset assertion in its own right instead of being handed to the count detector, which reads only the noun phrase and ignores the numerator; (2) the all-but branch reserves its whole span even when the subset comes to one member, so RX_SUBSET can no longer reinterpret the phrase nested inside it with the opposite meaning; (3) a declaration's n and of CORROBORATE the printed figures and never replace them, and decide alone only for a fragment with no N-of-M phrase in it; (4) an item's edges are stripped as punctuation and then as a conjunction WORD, because strip(" ;.,and") is a character set; (5) parse_enumeration keeps every completed run with the position that ended it and takes the longest, so a trailing cross reference no longer erases the list; (6) compound tens are read first and blanked before the single-word scan; (7) RX_BARE_NUM takes the whole numeric token and integers only; (8) a separating term matches as a whole word or phrase with one optional inflection, via term_matches(). CODEX ROUND TWO (head 80792e7) closed two more: the digits-only RX_RATIO runs first and claimed the span of "9 of 10 items ask about the payload", so verify_subset never saw it, and `ratio` proves the arithmetic and never reads a predicate or a separating term. A ratio whose counted universe IS one claim's parsed enumeration is now refused and has to be declared as a subset, and covers() lets a subset declaration answer for a ratio detection so the honest author has a path. parse_enumeration's tie now goes to the LATER run, which is what its own paragraph promised; bare max() returns the first maximal element. CODEX ROUND FOUR (head c18634a) found the reason this gate had never actually read this deck's own payoff sentence, and it was not the grammar: rendered_strings() read node["text"], which render.py caps at EIGHTY characters for display, instead of node["full"], the whole one-line textContent at 400 that copy_sync_check already uses. Every assertion past character 80 of a paragraph was invisible. The subset grammar also now covers a bare "all N" and "N out of M", not only the "of the" construction.

entries.change: dossier_check.py now compares each dossier's field 7 (Technique stack) against that slide's own <script> tags and dynamic imports: a library named in backticks must be loaded by the frame. It resolves bare names against assets/js, the four aliases (d3, topojson, zdog, three) and the global handles that belong to exactly one library, so `AKT.snapshot` names akthree as surely as the filename does. `AK` is deliberately not attributable, because noise.js, aktype.js, aklabel.js, akrelief.js and akhachure.js all publish into it. One direction only, like the contact promise: using something the dossier never mentioned is unremarkable, promising something the frame can't contain is the defect. CODEX ROUND (PR #391): libs_loaded strips HTML comments before matching, so an obsolete commented-out script tag no longer counts as loaded. That is the likeliest way this gate would have been fooled, because a commented-out tag is exactly what an abandoned technique leaves behind, which is the same moment the dossier goes stale. CODEX ROUND TWO (head 80792e7): libs_loaded reads the whole import ARGUMENT and counts any .js string literal in it, so the computed form this repo actually uses, `await import(A + '/js/akthree.js')`, is recognised alongside the quoted literal. CODEX ROUND FOUR: JS line and block comments are stripped from SCRIPT BODIES before the import scan, so `// import('/js/akthree.js')` no longer counts as loaded. A line comment is not recognised after a colon, so a https:// url survives.

entries.verification: RECONSTRUCTION, tests/technique_stack_verify.py, five fixtures against one slide that loads aksection.js, akengrave.js and akpost.js -> HOLDS. 02 names `akthree` (run No.64's own claim) -> FAIL naming akthree.js. 03 names no filename but writes `AKT.snapshot`, which is exactly how the claim survived the round-three sweep, the token renamed and the handle left behind -> FAIL naming akthree.js. NEGATIVE CONTROLS: 01 names what it loads, 04 writes `AK.grainTile` (the shared namespace, not attributable, the gate must not guess), 05 is prose with no backticked library at all -> all three clean, and clean of any other finding too. THEN IT FOUND TWO LIVE RESIDUALS OF ITS OWN DEFECT IN THE SHIPPED PLAN, which the round-three sweep and five critics missed: slide 01's field 7 still carried `AKT.environment` inside a bullet relabelled `aksection` but never rewritten (it still described procedural IBL, a 2048 px PCFSoft shadow map, ACES and `AKT.snapshot`, none of which that frame does), and slide 03's field 7 and field 5 both promised `akhachure` (#92) 'beyond the cut' where the frame draws a far ridge silhouette in graded fog and loads no hachure library at all. Both corrected in out/2026-09-20/storyboard.md to name what shipped, after which dossier_check is PASS 9 of 9, 0 fails 0 warns. NOT corrected in runs/2026-09-20/storyboard.md: a shipped artifact is never rewritten, and no pixel moved either way, this is a planning document telling the truth about a deck that is already correct. Pre-change dossier_check on the corrected storyboard is also PASS, so nothing else moved. BOTH DECKS through the real engine as above. CODEX ROUND: tests/technique_stack_verify.py gained fixture 06, a dossier naming `akthree` over a slide whose akthree.js tag sits inside `<!-- ... -->`. Against the PRE-FIX dossier_check it PASSES, which is the hole; against the fixed one it FAILS naming akthree.js. All six fixtures HOLD. dossier_check still reads PASS 9 of 9, 0 fails 0 warns on this run's corrected storyboard. CODEX ROUND TWO, and this one was a FALSE FAILURE, which is the worse kind: run against runs/2026-09-01, whose five akthree slides all build the module path from a variable inside glRow(), the check reported that slide 01's field 7 named `AKT.objectHero` while the slide never loaded akthree.js. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY ARCHIVED RUN, which is the number that says whether this is safe to ship: 13 runs under runs/ shipped their slide HTML, and the check produced 21 findings BEFORE the fix and 20 AFTER. Each finding was triaged by asking whether the named library's FILE is referenced in that slide at all: 1 FALSE and 20 TRUE before, 0 FALSE and 20 TRUE after. The 20 that remain are the defect this gate exists for, found retrospectively in four archived decks (2026-09-02 AKT.webglOK, 2026-09-04 five AKSNOW, 2026-09-09 seven AKNIGHT plus AKGeo and AKENGRAVE.surface, 2026-09-11 akhachure twice, akrelief and akengrave), every one of them a library whose file appears nowhere in the frame. tests/technique_stack_verify.py gained fixture 07, the computed path, and now carries 7 and HOLDS; 07 FAILS against 80792e7 and is clean now. A CORRECTION TO THE ROUND-ONE RECORD: the first proof of the HTML-comment fixture was run with the old script copied to a scratch directory that had no assets/ beside it, so library_files() was empty and EVERY finding vanished, which made fixture 06 look like it failed for the right reason when it failed for no reason. Re-run properly against 31e9ef79 with assets present, fixture 06 is CLEAN there, which is the hole, and fails correctly from 80792e7 onward. The conclusion is unchanged; the evidence for it now exists. CODEX ROUND FOUR: tests/technique_stack_verify.py gained fixture 08, a slide whose only akthree import is inside a `//` comment and whose aksnow one is inside a `/* */` block, with a https:// url in the same script as the trap for a careless line-comment strip. It passes against HEAD c18634a, which is the hole, and fails naming akthree.js now. Eight fixtures, HOLDS. THE 13-ARCHIVED-RUN SWEEP WAS RE-RUN: 20 findings, 0 FALSE, 20 TRUE, unchanged from the computed-path fix, so the comment strip costs nothing in false failures and closes the evasion. DECLINED in the same pass, recorded in the retro: a field 7 that writes the library FILENAME, `akthree.js` rather than `akthree`, is a real gap and has never happened. The 13-run sweep is the measurement and not one of its 20 findings is a filename token.

entries.change: assets/js/akpost.js's usage block now states that EVERY grading option is sticky and that there is no dither-only call: it lists the non-identity defaults grade() supplies when you omit them (filmic true, saturation 1.06, contrast 1.10) and gives the explicit incantation for adding dither and nothing else. Documentation only; not one line of behaviour changed, because every shipped deck's look depends on those defaults. Round two also fixed the aksection ribbon resample this run's own Codex pass had left half done: the guard was `total / (pts.length - 1) > DENSE`, so a two point ribbon 6 design px or shorter skipped the resample and went back to sampling only t = 0 and t = 1, where widthAt is zero by construction. A two point path is now always resampled, to at least 4 segments. Round four also fixed incise()'s lip: the up-light shoulder was chosen ONCE for the whole path from the mean of its vertex normals, and locator() passes a CLOSED RECTANGLE for the window, whose normals sum to roughly zero. The shoulder is now chosen from each segment's own normal against the key.
entries.trigger: Run No.64 round two. The risk register named IGN dither as the mitigation for a 900 px sky ramp; adding what looked like a dither-only call, `AKPOST.grade(cx, {w, h, dither: true})`, ran the full ACES curve over every frame (akpost.js line 223 is `const filmic = o.filmic !== false`), took slide 06 from clean to nine label-crossing failures in one render, and silently invalidated the contact, contrast and encoding numbers already measured off the previous render. The usage block showed `dither: true` inside a full options object and read like a list of what you are passing rather than a list of what you get. The ribbon guard is Codex's finding on head 80792e7: the comment promised an interior sample whatever the caller passed and the code delivered one only for long enough inputs.
entries.verification: Comment-only hunk; akpost.js still loads and AKPOST.grade is a function under node. BOTH DECKS re-rendered and re-graded AFTER the edit, because it is a shared asset and the engine's staleness gate is right to insist: this run's 9 slides render 9/9 OK, qa.py 0 fails / 0 warns PASS; examples/demo-deck 4/4 OK, qa.py 0 fails / 14 warns WARN. Identical to the pre-edit readings. Deliberately NOT done: changing the default. Flipping `filmic` would restyle every deck this studio has published, and that is the maintainer's call, not a retro's. RIBBON FIX: tests/ribbon_taper_verify.py drives the REAL AKSECT.ribbon through a stub 2D context and measures the shoelace area of what was filled, against the shipped library and against a reconstruction of it with only that one condition put back. HOLDS. A 4 px two point ribbon measured 3.6e-12 px2 before and 30.74 px2 after; a 1 px one 1.8e-12 before and 7.68 after; the 40 px size the locator ticks actually are measured 334.93 px2 before AND after, to the last digit, and a five point path 343.93 before and after. So the fix reaches only the inputs that were drawing nothing. PROVED ON THE DECK TOO: all nine of this run's frames re-rendered BYTE-IDENTICAL by md5 to the render made before the change, with a control pair of identical-code renders establishing that this engine is deterministic frame for frame. qa.py 0 fails 0 warns PASS; examples/demo-deck 4/4 OK, 0 fails 14 warns WARN. PER-SEGMENT LIP: tests/ribbon_taper_verify.py gained two fixtures that score every lip vertex on whether its displacement from the path runs WITH the key. On a closed rectangle, the locator window, 60 percent of lip vertices were up-light before and 100 percent are now; on an open diagonal groove, which the mean always got right, 100 percent before AND after. Six fixtures, HOLDS. This one DOES move pixels, unlike the ribbon fix, and the amount is measured rather than asserted: all nine frames change, by 0.38 to 1.52 percent of their pixels, mean 0.61 percent, confined to the groove bevels. qa.py reads 0 fails and 0 warns on all nine after it, and examples/demo-deck is 4/4 OK with 0 fails and 14 warns, unchanged. assemble.py re-run so out/2026-09-20/final matches the new render; runs/2026-09-20 is untouched.

entries.change: scripts/gmail_draft.py's sign-off table now prints verdicts instead of the artifact index, and reads the block Phase 3.6 actually writes. Two faults, one section. First, run_state's `artifacts` maps each phase to a LIST OF FILENAMES, which is that field's documented shape, so artifacts['gas_watch'] is always a list of paths; `_look` rejected dicts and accepted everything else, so the list answered ahead of the real verdict and its repr landed in the cell. Only a scalar can be a line, so only a scalar is accepted now. Second, this run recorded Phase 3.6 under run_state['phase_3_6'] with the phase's own key names, a shape no earlier run had used and nothing read, so the rows that would have been right were invisible; the flatten now reads it, mapping gaswatch_live to the live verdict and gaswatch_pagecheck to the local one, which leaves the existing rule that the live audit outranks the local page check deciding as before. A CRON HEALTH row was added alongside, and it is explicitly excluded from the UNREPORTED guard's count so no extra row can ever stand in for a missing site sign-off. ROUND FIVE closed the half of it the first cut missed: a single artifact PATH is no more a verdict than a list of them. 2026-09-19's artifacts.cron_health is the bare string out/2026-09-19/cron_health.json while its phase_3_6.cron_health is PASS, so the new CRON HEALTH row printed the filename and suppressed the verdict. _look now refuses anything that parses as a path to a file, whatever its type, which covers every label rather than the one that happened to show it. The suite's archive sweep was widened to match: it had rejected only list reprs and quoted .json strings, which is exactly why it missed this. The suite is also hermetic now, through gmail_draft.py's new GMAIL_DRAFT_NO_NETWORK switch: the readership section shells out to read_stats.py with a 60 second timeout, and at 70 renders a half-open endpoint would have turned a bounded test into a half-hour one issuing dozens of live requests. Round five also took two findings on scripts/aggregate_check.py. A declaration with no "fragment" covers every detection whose fragment sits inside its text while verify() reads that text with one .search(), so a node printing two subset assertions was covered twice and checked once: such a declaration is now refused by name and told to give an exact fragment. And "selected" is required to be a list of whole numbers, because Python iterates a string without complaining, so selected: "34" became the indices 3 and 4 and validated a printed two-item subset by accident. ROUND SIX closed the ambiguity fix's own gap. detect() keyed its dedupe on the fragment TEXT, so two DISTINCT assertions printing the same phrase ("Two of the four items name the air and the land. Two of the four items name the dock and the roads.") collapsed into one hit: the second was never detected, let alone verified, and a correct declaration for the first returned a clean PASS over it. Detection is per OCCURRENCE now, keyed on the match offset as well, which still collapses the same span caught twice. The ambiguity rule counts occurrences WITHIN ONE rendered node, because a number printed in four places on a slide is one assertion said four times and is correctly answered by one declaration: the first cut of this rule refused run No.64's own slide 02, which prints "10 days" in four nodes.
entries.trigger: Phase 13 of run No.64, reading the built body before creating the draft. The table read "GAS WATCH ['out/2026-09-20/gaswatch_health.json', 'out/2026-09-20/cron_health.json']" and carried no SITE SIGN-OFF row at all, on a day the live gas watch audit returned MAINTENANCE and the site sign-off returned WARN with an UNFIXED finding. Both verdicts existed and both were in run_state. This is the fourth costume of the bug this section's own comments already document three of: a report that omits the warning while still looking complete. The UNREPORTED guard could not catch it either, because the filename list counted as a substantive answer. The new test found the same repr had shipped in the drafts for runs 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-20.
entries.verification: tests/gmail_signoff_verify.py, 19 checks, HOLDS, hermetic. Every check was proven red against the pre-fix script first, including three real shipped runs (2026-08-08, 2026-08-20, 2026-09-20) for the list form and runs/2026-09-19 for the single-path form. The suite renders a real draft body per fixture and reads the table out of the emitted bytes, because this section is prose built at write time where no static check reaches it, and it renders all 64 shipped run_state files. The pre-existing shapes are pinned: top-level scalars (2026-09-17) and the one-dict form (2026-08-25). tests/subset_assert_verify.py carries the two aggregate_check fixes at 29 fixtures: 5 ambiguous, 5 selected_str, 5 selected_frac and 6 same_frag are each red against the gate of the round before them, and two positive controls hold the rule off correct work: 5 fragmented proves the exact "fragment" escape hatch still passes, and 6 two_nodes proves one phrase printed in two different nodes is still one assertion. entries.change: qa.py's axis census takes its ORIGIN from the clamped sample start rather than from the declared minimum, in both axis_census() and _census_band_hunt(). The census already cut its sample window to the frame (r0 = max(0, int(lo * ns))) and then indexed that profile from the unclamped `lo`, so a slide declaring an axis endpoint OFF the frame -- the correct declaration for a camera that has descended past its own scale -- had every peak_at(p), every nearest-ink search and every undeclared-mark position read at an index offset by exactly the amount clamped. One line each; _census_band_hunt's origin_perp two lines above was already doing the same division correctly, which is the pattern that was copied.

entries.change: The scout's PDF reader is hardened and its guard ships, and the Bash grant that would let a scout run it is NOT in place. scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py now puts one address policy (the new scripts/url_safety.py) on the first URL and on every redirect hop, refusing anything that is not a public http(s) destination, and bounds the whole transfer including the connect and header phase, which a per-read timeout never covered. scripts/scout_bash_guard.py is a default-deny PreToolUse hook that would allow exactly one command, python3 scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py <url> with its read-only flags, and deny everything else including --out, the only flag that makes that script write a file. .claude/agents/scout.md keeps WebSearch, WebFetch and Read, and its brief now tells a scout it has no shell and to fall back to the HTML rendering of a PDF. UNTESTED IN A LIVE SCOUT: the grant was withheld after eight rounds of review found a bypass in each of the first six, the last a reproduced DNS rebinding that needs the socket pinned to the address that was validated. The one line that re-enables it, and the three conditions to meet first, are in a comment at the top of scout.md.
entries.trigger: Run No.66's six scouts had no Bash tool, so the PDF reader every scout brief has named since No.62 was unreachable. Four of six said so in dead_ends and several primary documents went unread, among them the DNR preliminary decision for ADL 234762, AIDEA's development plan and fact sheet, the AI3 NOFO and the 36 MB draft 2027-2030 STIP. The showrunner ran the identical command by hand and it worked first time on both Mat-Su PDFs, which is the only reason the deck had primary sources. A claim that is never made can't fail the claims gate, so an unreadable primary document is a silent hole in it: claims_check passed 38 of 38 while four beats read secondary coverage of documents they had already found. Plain Bash was rejected (six leaf workers at once, Bash allowed outright in settings.json, and an unrestricted shell can write the repo or start another agent process, which is the fan-out non-negotiable 7 exists to stop); a showrunner pre-fetch was rejected on the acceptance test; an MCP server was rejected because a trust prompt in a routine run is a stop and a stop is a failed run; a permissions.deny rule was rejected because deny rules bind the showrunner too.
entries.verification: scout_bash_guard.py --self-test PASS: 9 allowed command shapes, 22 denied (python3 -c, --out in both spellings, ; && | and > chaining, cd prefix, command substitution in $() and backticks, a quoted $HOME path, claude -p, curl, bash as the interpreter, another repo script, two positional urls, an unknown flag, an unterminated quote, echo, empty), plus a wiring check that FAILS if scout.md loses the hook block or its tools line gains Task, Write, Edit or NotebookEdit. Exercised as a real hook over stdin: the scout's own command exits 0, python3 -c exits 2 with the reason, unparseable stdin exits 2 (fail closed). scout.md frontmatter parsed as YAML and checked against the hooks schema Claude Code enforces (PreToolUse -> [{matcher, hooks:[{type: command, command, timeout}]}]); the running claude binary contains the agent-hooks parser. python3 scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py on the Mat-Su ordinance PDF returned the ordinance text at exit 0, which is the acceptance test minus the scout process. (1) SLOPE-AND-ASPECT HACHURE SHADING, the finding that answers our standing weakness. Woodruff's sketchy-relief method is browser canvas with no dependencies: grid the height field, compute slope and aspect per cell, draw one stroke per cell with WIDTH encoding slope and ROTATION encoding aspect, make strokes longer than the cell so neighbours blend, jitter positions and bend strokes so the field reads drawn rather than stamped, then redraw the whole field several times at low opacity with the sun angle varied slightly so shadow detail ACCUMULATES. Why it matters here: our TOOTH and stipple fields are parameterised by POSITION, so a density falloff is a gradient over an otherwise identical texture, and this run proved for the second time that a reader cannot see it (the declared falloff ran in code and was invisible in every render per two pixel critics and the scorer). A hachure field is parameterised by the DATA UNDER IT, so the non-uniformity is structural rather than applied. PARKED: it wants a TECHNIQUE_LIBRARY entry with our own parameters and one trial slide judged at 432px before a director is told to reach for it. (2) HUMAN-RECOGNISABLE OBJECTS IN THE THUMB. scan_log.found: ORACLE ANCHORING (arXiv:2608.17214, 'Oracles That Cannot Fail'). A test oracle that takes its expected value from the system it judges can't fail, because a fault moves measurement and expectation together and the comparison cancels. Specification-anchored expectations come from values fixed outside the thing under test; state-anchored ones flow from it. Measured on a deployed air traffic simulator: re-anchoring one oracle on published procedure, changing no production code, recovered 8 of 46 missed mutants, and state-anchoring a healthy one cost 4 of 19. This names this studio's oldest review defect better than the studio has: dossier_check.py's own docstring says 'the pixel critics grade each slide against its OWN dossier, so a slide that executed a bad plan passes its acceptance checklist', which is a state-anchored oracle, and run No.37 produced two textbook instances (Device B promised to cut a data object with the right frame edge when the plate ends at x1040 and the frame at x1080; Device C, declared a FIXED title block, shipped at eight different heights). Supporting result: arXiv:2608.17177 measures that making an agent write pre- and post-conditions BEFORE generating tests improves bug detection 9.8 points (p 0.0352), which is the declare-then-measure pattern this run's contact-shadow fix uses.

Computer-generated hillshade gives a lowland ridge the same graphic weight as a summit, which is a plausible cause of the flat busy lower thirds that keep earning frame-balance warns here. (1) WEIGHTED SAMPLE ELIMINATION (Yuksel, EUROGRAPHICS 2015) turns any dense seeded candidate set into a blue-noise subset of a target size with no radius chosen up front and with an optional density function, so a population reads as measured rather than as grain AT THE SAME COUNT. Parameters read out of the reference implementation and not the abstract: 2D r_max = sqrt(A / (2*sqrt(3)*N)), d_max = 2*r_max, weight = sum of (1 - d/d_max)^alpha over neighbours inside d_max with alpha 8, weight-limit fraction (1 - (N_out/N_in)^gamma)*beta with beta 0.65 and gamma 1.5. A uniform grid replaces the kd-tree at our counts, so about 100 lines of vanilla JS and no dependency. (2) JOBARD AND LEFER evenly-spaced streamline placement (1997) makes flow-field density a single parameter d_sep, with d_test = 0.5*d_sep and new seeds offered perpendicular at d_sep from each finished line, plus a multiresolution variant that fills gaps with the coarse lines frozen. Both are the honest answer to a field or population that is dense in one quadrant and bald in another. Sources: cemyuksel.com/research/sampleelimination, github.com/cemyuksel/cyCodeBase/blob/master/cySampleElim.h, semanticscholar Jobard-Lefer 1997, bookofshapes.com/patterns/flow_lines.

scan_log.found: EROSION IS THE ONE LAND-SURFACE TECHNIQUE THIS HOUSE HAS NEVER BUILT. Two of the three usual answers are already mined out here: domain warping is AK.warp2 in noise.js and is what akrelief defaults to at strength 0.5, and ridged multifractal is already in TECHNIQUE_LIBRARY. What is absent is erosion, which is what puts concave valley floors under convex ridges and is the difference between a noise field and land. Two algorithms with parameters, and for an engraved SECTION the second is the better buy: droplet hydraulic (Lague's defaults, radius 3, inertia 0.05, capacity factor 4, erode/deposit 0.3, evaporate 0.01, gravity 4, lifetime 30) which produces dendritic drainage and is a plan-view pleasure; and THERMAL EROSION, the talus-angle model, which moves Kt * (Hmax / 2) to the lower neighbours in proportion to their height difference but only where the slope exceeds R(x,y) * Ka + Ki. The half is the anti-oscillation term, not a tuning choice. Thermal is a handful of neighbour passes rather than tens of thousands of droplets, it converges instead of needing a budget, it makes the crisp ridgelines and constant-angle scree a drawn bluff actually has, and its hardness field R(x,y) is an honest hook for a story quantity the way akengrave's `form` already is. Sources: https://github.com/SebLague/Hydraulic-Erosion/blob/master/Assets/Scripts/Erosion.cs , https://old.cescg.org/CESCG-2011/papers/TUBudapest-Jako-Balazs.pdf , https://github.com/dandrino/terrain-erosion-3-ways
